name: Hub
tagline: Two channels of poly CV processing with a big hands-on knob, a voltmeter and a corn cob display.

sections.panelMap:
HUB is a macro controller and CV processing hub. Each of the two channels has gain, offset and a VCA, for poly signals. The display reads out the output voltage, and the big animated knob follows the input; grab it to take over and set the CV by hand. The corn cob display shows the voltage of every poly channel.

Each channel (I and II):
- Input jack, with two small knobs: gain (-2x to +2x, so you can invert or boost) and offset (±10V).
- Big knob: shows the input after gain and offset. Turn it yourself to override the input and set the CV by hand.
- Display: the voltage of the first output channel.
- VCA knob, attenuverter and CV: the output range, 0–10V. Patch CV here to use it as a VCA.
- Output: the result, polyphonic.
- Corn cob: one kernel per poly channel. Large yellow kernels are positive voltages, small white ones negative.
sections.basicUse:
1. Patch CV into a channel's input.
2. Set gain and offset to fit the range you need.
3. Read the result on the display, or watch the corn cob for poly signals.
4. Grab the big knob any time to take over by hand.
5. Patch an envelope into the VCA CV to fade the channel in and out.
sections.patching:
• Range adapter: Turn a 0–10V envelope into ±5V with gain 1 and offset -5V.

• Performance controls: Put HUB at the front of a patch with its outputs on the most important parameters. Let modulation run, and grab the knobs when you want to steer.

• Poly VCA: Patch a poly modulation source in and a single envelope into the VCA CV to fade all voices together.

• Voltmeter: Patch anything in to read its voltage and see its poly channels.

name: CV funk Blank 8HP
tagline: An 8HP CV funk blank panel.

sections.panelMap: An 8HP blank panel with the CV funk look. It has no controls.
sections.basicUse: Use it to space out your rack.

name: CV funk Blank 4HP
tagline: A 4HP CV funk blank panel.

sections.panelMap: A 4HP blank panel with the CV funk look. It has no controls.
sections.basicUse: Use it to space out your rack.

name: Rat
tagline: A polyphonic ratio generator for FM. The knob spends most of its travel near the ratios that sound good.

sections.panelMap:
RAT is a polyphonic ratio generator for exploring FM. Patch in the pitch of one oscillator and RAT outputs the pitch of a second at a set ratio. The RATIO knob isn't linear: it gives you the most precision around useful, slightly detuned ratios.

Jacks and controls:
- OSC I V/OCT: polyphonic pitch input for the first oscillator. It sets the module's polyphony.
- Display: the current ratio. Normally it shows three decimal places, so you can see the detune. With LOCK on, it shows the ratio as a fraction.
- LOCK: snaps to whole fractional ratios.
- RATIO: ±16. Values above 1 multiply, below -1 divide, and the region from -1 to 1 is 1:1. Has an attenuverter and CV.
- OSC II V/OCT: polyphonic pitch output, scaled by the ratio.

Context menu:
- Ratio Non-Linearity: how strongly the knob favours ratios near whole numbers. LOCK overrides it and outputs the nearest fixed ratio.
sections.basicUse:
1. Patch your carrier's pitch into OSC I V/OCT, and OSC II V/OCT into your modulator.
2. Turn RATIO to choose the relationship. Small moves near a whole number give gentle detuning and slow beating.
3. Press LOCK for exact ratios like 3:2 or 7:4.
sections.patching:
• FM ratio: Run two oscillators from RAT and FM one with the other. Sweep RATIO for classic DX-style timbres.

• Beating pairs: Set RATIO just off 2.000 and mix the two oscillators for slow phasing.

• Poly FM: Patch a poly V/oct in. Every voice gets its modulator at the same ratio.

• Several operators: Chain more RATs from the same input for a stack of ratios.

videos.title: New Modules, November 2025

name: Count
tagline: A counter with a big display. Counts up, down, in loops or forever, and outputs gates and a stepped phase.

sections.panelMap:
COUNT is a counting module with a large display. Loop, stop at the ends, or count forever. It outputs a gate at the boundaries and a stepped phase voltage.

Display: the current number. The font shrinks to fit as the number grows.

Counting:
- UP, DOWN, RESET: add one, subtract one, or reset. Each has a button and an input.
- LOOP / ∞ / STOP switch: Loop wraps around within MAX VAL. Unbounded (∞) keeps counting without limit, up to a 64-bit integer. Stop holds at the ends of the range.
- RESET POINT switch: reset to zero, the midpoint, or the end.
- MAX VAL: type in any positive number up to 14 digits.

Outputs:
- GATE: goes high at the loop point (Loop) or at the ends (Stop).
- PHASE: 0–10V stepped voltage showing where the count sits relative to MAX VAL. In Unbounded mode it cycles.

Context menu:
- Zero-based counting (start at 0): counts 0–9 instead of 1–10 for a MAX VAL of 10. Useful for linking several counters into a bigger display.
sections.basicUse:
1. Type a MAX VAL.
2. Patch a clock into UP.
3. Pick Loop, Unbounded or Stop.
4. Take GATE as a trigger every MAX VAL counts, and PHASE as a stepped ramp.
sections.patching:
• Clock divider: MAX VAL 16 in Loop mode. GATE fires once every 16 clocks.

• Sequencer address: Patch PHASE into a switch or a sequencer's CV input to step through positions in order.

• Up and down: Patch two different clocks into UP and DOWN. The count drifts in whichever direction is faster.

• Bigger counters: Turn on zero-based counting and patch one COUNT's GATE into the next one's UP to count into the millions.

• Countdown: Set the reset point to End, Stop mode, and clock DOWN. GATE fires when it reaches zero.

videos.title: New Modules, November 2025

name: Clpy
tagline: A stereo polyphonic waveshaper that folds small signals and clips big ones toward a voltage you choose.

sections.panelMap:
CLPY folds your waves and clips them toward a target voltage. Quiet parts of a signal go through a smooth sine fold. As the level rises past about 4.6V, the output crossfades toward the CLIP voltage instead of a hard rail. Because CLIP is under CV, you can clip to a moving voltage, or even to another audio signal.

Controls:
- IN L / R: stereo input, polyphonic.
- GAIN: input gain, 0–10x, with attenuverter and CV. More gain means more folding and more clipping.
- CLIP: the target voltage, ±5V, with attenuverter.
- CLIP L / R inputs: CV or audio for the clip target on each side. If only one is patched, it's used for both.
- OUT L / R.

Context menu:
- Clipping Mode: Convergent (default) sends both halves of the wave toward CLIP. Symmetric sends the positive half to +CLIP and the negative half to -CLIP, like a classic clipper.
- Supersampling: oversampled processing for less aliasing. The CLIP input is smoothed too, so fast CV and audio into CLIP stay clean.
- Bandlimit Filter: a 6-pole low-pass after the shaper, with a Filter Cutoff slider.
sections.basicUse:
1. Patch audio into IN and take OUT.
2. Raise GAIN until the signal starts folding and clipping.
3. Set CLIP to choose where the clipped parts land. At 0V in Convergent mode, loud parts fold back toward silence.
4. Try Symmetric mode for a more familiar clipper sound.
5. Turn on Supersampling for clean high-gain results.
sections.patching:
• Clip to an envelope: Patch an envelope into CLIP L. Loud parts of the signal follow the envelope shape.

• Clip to audio: Patch a second oscillator into CLIP. The loud parts of the first take on the second, for ring-mod-like timbres.

• Stereo width: Send different LFOs into CLIP L and CLIP R.

• Gentle warmth: GAIN just above 1 and CLIP near 0V adds soft harmonics without obvious clipping.

name: Tuner
tagline: Two tuners side by side, each with a waveform display and a V/oct output.

sections.panelMap:
TUNER is two independent pitch detectors, each with its own display. Each display shows the note name with its offset in cents, the frequency in Hz, and the waveform, held steady across a set number of cycles.

Each channel:
- IN: audio to measure.
- OFFSET: moves the waveform up or down on the display, ±5V.
- GAIN: scales the waveform on the display, 0–5x.
- WIDTH: how many cycles to show, 1–6.
- V/OCT: the detected pitch as V/oct.
GAIN, OFFSET and WIDTH only change the display, not the measurement.

Context menu:
- Analysis speed: trade response time for CPU.
- Large Hz display (disable waveform): replaces the waveform with a big frequency readout.
sections.basicUse:
1. Patch an oscillator into IN.
2. Read the note and cents offset at the top of the display.
3. Use GAIN, OFFSET and WIDTH to get a clear view of the waveform.
4. Take V/OCT to use the detected pitch elsewhere.
sections.patching:
• Tuning oscillators: Patch an oscillator in and tune it until the cents read zero. Use both channels to tune two oscillators against each other.

• Checking V/oct tracking: Play octaves into an oscillator and watch whether the note stays on pitch.

• Pitch follower: Patch V/OCT into a quantizer or another oscillator to follow the pitch of any sound.

name: Alloy
tagline: Strike a ring of tuned delay lines for bells, cymbals and metal. Polyphonic and stereo.

sections.panelMap:
ALLOY is a metallic voice built from a ring of Karplus-Strong delay lines. A strike sends a short noise burst into the ring. Each node is tuned slightly differently and panned across the stereo field, and their outputs run through ADAA saturation. The result ranges from tuned bells and plates to cymbals and clangs. Patch audio into IN and the ring becomes a resonator for other sounds.

Pitch:
- PITCH knob and V/oct input: ±4V around C4. A poly V/oct gives each voice its own ring.

Tone (each with an attenuverter and CV):
- SHAPE: how the nodes are tuned. Negative scatters them into a chaotic, cymbal-like cluster; positive spreads them evenly for a clearer metallic shimmer.
- TEMPER: coupling between neighbouring nodes. More coupling gives a more blended, sympathetic ring.
- RESONANCE: feedback in the ring, which sets how long it rings.
- OVERDRIVE: saturation after the nodes.

Strike section:
- STRIKE button and input: fires the noise burst.
- IMPULSE: length of the burst.
- NOISE: a little noise fed in continuously while the ring sounds, for sizzle.

Jacks:
- IN: audio into the ring.
- VOLUME, and OUT L / R.

Context menu:
- Set Node Count: 4, 8, 12 (default) or 16 nodes.
- Delay effect mode: drops the pitch range by 4 octaves so the ring becomes long delay lines, for using ALLOY as an effect.
sections.basicUse:
1. Press STRIKE or patch a trigger into it.
2. Set the pitch with PITCH, or play it from a V/oct source.
3. Turn SHAPE to move between cymbal-like chaos and clear metal.
4. Set the ring time with RESONANCE.
5. Add TEMPER for a richer, more blended tone, and OVERDRIVE for grit.
sections.patching:
• Metal percussion: Trigger it from a gate sequencer. SHAPE positive and moderate RESONANCE for bells, SHAPE negative for cymbals and hats.

• Resonator: Patch drums or a plucked sound into IN and tune PITCH to the key of your track.

• Poly bells: Patch poly V/oct and poly gates in for a resonator per note.

• Dense swells: SHAPE fully negative, TEMPER high, RESONANCE moderate, with a little NOISE.

• Metallic delay: Turn on Delay effect mode and feed audio into IN.

name: Onion
tagline: Eighteen sliders, eighteen outputs, and a LAYERS knob that turns each output into a poly stack.

sections.panelMap:
ONION is a bank of 18 sliders, each with its own output. The LAYERS knob makes every output polyphonic: each one carries its own slider plus the next ones in line, so a single cable can carry a whole stack of values. That's the onion, in layers.

Controls:
- −/+ and + switch: bipolar (−DEPTH to +DEPTH) or unipolar (0 to DEPTH). Switching moves the sliders so the voltages stay the same.
- LAYERS: 1–16 channels on each output. Output N carries sliders N, N+1, N+2 and so on, wrapping around after 18.
- DEPTH knob and CV: the full-scale voltage of the sliders, up to 10V.
- 18 sliders in three rows of six, each with its output in the bar below.
sections.basicUse:
1. Choose bipolar or unipolar, and set DEPTH.
2. Set the sliders.
3. With LAYERS at 1, use the outputs as 18 separate CV sources.
4. Turn LAYERS up to get poly stacks from each output.
sections.patching:
• Chord shapes: Set LAYERS to 4 and use the sliders as pitches. Each output is a different four-note chord made of neighbouring sliders.

• Poly voice settings: Set LAYERS to the number of voices in a poly patch and use the sliders as per-voice settings like detune or pan.

• Macro fade: Patch an envelope into DEPTH to scale all 18 outputs together.

name: Strata
tagline: A layered pitch sequencer with a drum-pattern heart. Rhythm, pitch, semitone and octave rows that each move at their own pace.

sections.panelMap:
STRATA is a step sequencer built in layers. A rhythm generator in the style of PICUS decides when notes happen. A row of eight pitch knobs decides what they are. A semitone row and an octave row add variation on top, each stepping at its own rate. Four complete layers can be stored and switched.

Transport:
- PATTERN LEN.: length of the beat pattern, 1–24, with CV.
- CLOCK and RESET (with a button).
- PLAY MODE: 0 (off), I (on), or 1 (one-shot).

Rhythm (top):
- Pattern lights: up to 24 steps, each DON, KA or off. Click to change them.
- Eight stages, each with − / + button pairs for BEATS and CYCLES, shown as two numbers. A stage plays BEATS beats over CYCLES clocks. 0 cycles skips the stage; 0 beats mutes it.

Pitch:
- STEP / STAGE switch (STAGE, HYBRID, STEP): how the pattern and pitches move. In STAGE mode the pattern advances once per stage; in HYBRID it advances on every beat; in STEP mode every beat also steps the pitch, with DON beats moving through the left four knobs and KA beats through the right four.
- Eight pitch knobs, ±2V, in a left half and a right half, each with an on/off light.

Semitone row:
- Seven knobs, ±12 semitones, each with an on/off light, and its own BEATS and CYCLES.
- FWD / REV switch: forward, ping-pong or reverse.

Octave row:
- Four knobs, ±3 octaves, each with an on/off light, and its own BEATS and CYCLES.
- LT / RT switch: apply the octave to the left half, both halves, or the right half.

Layers:
- Four LAYER buttons, a next-layer button, and a LAYER CV input. Each layer stores its own knobs, beats and switches.
- OFFSET knob and CV: transposes everything, ±2V.

Outputs:
- Display: the note being played.
- INV, GATE and OUT.

Context menu:
- Copy Layer, Paste Layer, Paste to All Layers, and Paste Mode (Knobs + Beats, Knobs Only, Beats Only).
- Layer Advance by CV (1V/layer).
sections.basicUse:
1. Patch a clock into CLOCK and set PLAY MODE to I.
2. Set the beat pattern with the lights along the top, and PATTERN LEN.
3. Set the pitch knobs and switch on the ones you want.
4. Add the semitone and octave rows for variation, and set how often each steps.
5. Patch OUT to a V/oct input and GATE to an envelope.
6. Copy the layer to the other three and vary them. Switch layers by hand or with CV.
sections.patching:
• Evolving melody: Give each layer a different beat ratio and switch layers with LAYER CV at the start of each bar.

• Chromatic runs: Leave the main stages on long notes and run the semitone row faster for passing notes.

• Octave scenes: Run the octave row slowly to move the whole sequence up and down every few bars.

• One-shot phrases: Set PLAY MODE to 1 and trigger RESET to play the sequence once.

• Live variation: Click pattern steps between DON, KA and off while it plays.

name: Triton
tagline: A stereo three-band splitter with resonant crossovers, envelope followers and stereo width on any parameter.

sections.panelMap:
TRITON splits a stereo signal into low, mid and high bands. Each band has its own level, envelope follower and stereo outputs, and the bands also sum back together. A row of sliders sets the crossovers, and a WIDTH slider can push left and right apart on any of them for wide, moving stereo.

The display shows the filter response for left and right, the crossover points, and each band's envelope.

Inputs:
- IN L / R: audio. A mono signal in L goes to both sides.
- V/OCT: moves the crossovers to follow pitch.

Sliders (each with a trim and CV input below):
- CENTER: where the crossovers sit, tracked by V/OCT.
- SPREAD: distance between the two crossover points.
- GAP: negative overlaps the bands; positive leaves a gap of silence between them.
- SHARP: filter steepness, from 1 to 8 stages.
- RES.: a resonant peak at each crossover.
- DRIVE: tanh saturation before the split.
- WIDTH: offsets left against right on every slider whose button is lit.
The buttons above the first six sliders choose which ones WIDTH affects. Several can be on at once.

Band rows (LOW, MID, HIGH, MIX), each with:
- Level knob, with trim and CV.
- ENVELOPE output, with a light.
- L and R outputs. The MIX row's L and R carry all three bands summed.

Context menu:
- Internal Feedback: adds a feedback loop to the resonance for a stronger, wilder peak. Off by default.
- Scaled Envelopes: on by default, so each envelope output follows its band's level knob.
sections.basicUse:
1. Patch audio into IN L (and IN R for stereo).
2. Set CENTER and SPREAD to place the crossovers. Watch the display.
3. Take the bands from the LOW, MID and HIGH outputs, or the whole mix from MIX.
4. Use the level knobs to rebalance the bands.
5. Light a button and raise WIDTH to spread that parameter across left and right.
sections.patching:
• Multiband effects: Send each band to its own effect and mix them back together.

• Envelope followers: Use the ENVELOPE outputs to drive VCAs, filters or reverb sends elsewhere. The low band makes a good kick follower.

• Wide stereo: Light CENTER and raise WIDTH. Left and right crossovers move apart. Modulate WIDTH for movement.

• Moving notches: Set GAP high and SHARP steep for two deep notches, and sweep CENTER with an LFO.

• Resonant bass: Low CENTER, narrow SPREAD, RES. up, to pull a pitched sub out of a sound. Track it with V/OCT.

name: Aulos
tagline: A polyphonic double-pipe wind instrument. Morph from flute to reed, flare the bore into brass, and overblow into higher registers.

sections.panelMap:
AULOS is a physical model of a wind instrument, named after the ancient Greek double pipe. Each voice is a waveguide: a tube with waves travelling up and down it, reflecting at both ends. REED and BORE change those reflections directly, which reshapes the instrument itself. There are two pipes: MAIN, and a SECondary pipe you can tune to an interval or hold as a drone.

The display shows both tubes, MAIN on top and SEC. below. Each one shows its length, the breath filling it, a standing wave, its register and any overblow, with air streaming out of the bell and bursts of chiff on each attack. The bell flares with BORE, and the SEC. tube dims in drone mode.

Pitch: PIPE and FINGER
- PIPE input and knob (-1 to +4 octaves): the pipe's fundamental, the note the tube naturally wants to play. It doesn't have to follow the melody.
- FINGER input and knob (±1 octave): the fingering. This sets the tube's length, and the ratio of FINGER to PIPE sets the register. Around twice the PIPE pitch the tube overblows up an octave; around four times, up another. The change takes about 200 ms, so the tone morphs instead of jumping. Fingering below the pipe fundamental is allowed too, and gives a whistly low end.
- GATE input and button: polyphonic, up to 16 voices. The voice count follows the widest of GATE, FINGER and PIPE. The button holds the gate open for every voice.

Breath
- BREATH: breath pressure, with trim and CV. At zero there's no sound at all. Past a light threshold the note speaks and builds over its attack. More breath is louder and edgier, and at the top it pushes into overblow by itself.
- VIBRATO input and depth knob: with nothing patched, an internal LFO wobbles the pitch and the breath together. A patched CV replaces it and only moves the pitch.

Sliders (each with trim and CV)
- REED: flute to reed. At zero an air jet drives an open tube: the full harmonic series, breathy and hollow, like a flute. At the top a beating reed drives a closed tube: odd harmonics only, about an octave lower, buzzy and stable, like a clarinet. The middle is a crossover no real instrument has, with a sound all its own.
- BORE: the shape of the bell. Up to about 0.75 the tube widens like a clarinet body and the tone fills out without getting brighter. Past that it flares into a brass horn and brightens.
- DRIVE: saturation on the excitation only. The tube itself stays clean, so DRIVE adds harmonics without making the loop unstable.
- RES.: feedback in the tube. More resonance sustains more. If it squeals, turn it down.
- AIR: breath noise mixed into the excitation.
- CHIFF: the burst of air at the start of each note. Zero for none, up to a long, loud attack.
- SEC.: pitch of the second pipe, ±1 octave. Zero is unison, +0.585 a perfect fifth, +1 an octave.
- WOOD: damping inside the tube, from bright to warm and dark. It's scaled with register, so high notes keep their harmonics.

Other jacks
- DRONE button and input: locks the second pipe's gate on. It plays a little quieter than the main pipe and fades in and out without clicks. The input toggles it on each gate.
- EXT. IN and EXT. GAIN: feed audio into the tube to excite it from outside.
- VOLUME: output level, 0 to 3x, with trim and CV.
- ENVELOPE: the breath envelope, polyphonic, with a blue meter.
- RMS: a follower on the excitation, polyphonic, with a yellow meter.
- MAIN and SEC.: audio outputs for the two pipes. The second pipe only runs while SEC. is patched.

Context menu
- Aulos R Voice Mode: Tracking (interval preserved) keeps the second pipe at the same interval in every register. Two Pipes (fixed registers) lets each pipe find its own register from its own pitch.
- Resonator: Waveguide Gain (overall level into the tube) and Decay (ring-out after the gate falls).
- Envelope: Attack and Release times, and Envelope Curves for each (log to exponential).
- Vibrato: Rate (3–12 Hz) and Breath Coupling (how much the vibrato moves the breath as well as the pitch).
- Articulation: Legato. With a held gate, pitch changes slur instead of retriggering, with a little give in the tube at each slur. Legato Glide Time sets the glide.
- Dynamics Envelope: Follow Time for the RMS follower.
- Panic: Clear All Energy.
sections.basicUse:
1. Play a note:
   - Patch the same V/oct into PIPE and FINGER, and a gate into GATE. The tube plays at its fundamental.
   - Set BREATH. Too little and it won't speak; more makes it louder and edgier.

2. Choose the instrument:
   - REED low for flute, high for clarinet.
   - BORE above 0.75 for brass.
   - WOOD for a darker tone, DRIVE for more harmonics.

3. Add breath and attack:
   - AIR for breath noise, CHIFF for the tongued attack.

4. Overblow:
   - Send FINGER an octave above PIPE and the tube jumps to its next register, the way a real woodwind does.

5. Add the second pipe:
   - Patch SEC. and set the SEC. slider to an interval. Turn on DRONE to hold it while MAIN plays the melody.

6. Excite it with audio:
   - Patch a sound into EXT. IN and raise EXT. GAIN. The tube resonates at the PIPE pitch.
sections.patching:
• Flute melody: Same V/oct into PIPE and FINGER, REED near zero, DRIVE about 0.5, a little CHIFF.

• Reed lead: REED near the top. Add BORE past 0.75 for a brassier reed.

• Bore sweep: Sweep BORE from 0 to 1 with a slow LFO or envelope. The tone fills out, then flares into brass at the top, a morph no real instrument can make.

• Drone and melody: Patch SEC., set it to +0.585 (a fifth) or +1.0 (an octave), and turn on DRONE. The second pipe holds a drone under the melody and follows PIPE, so it stays in tune.

• Poly chords: Poly V/oct into FINGER and a poly gate into GATE. Every channel is a complete instrument with its own register.

• Crescendo from silence: Patch an expression pedal or slow envelope into BREATH CV. The note grows out of nothing. Use ENVELOPE to open a filter in step.

• Voice into the tube: Patch a vocal or formant sound into EXT. IN. The tube acts as a pitched resonator tuned by PIPE.

• Slurred phrases: Turn on Legato and keep the gate high while the pitch changes.

• Delayed vibrato: Automate the VIBRATO depth knob with a slow envelope so the vibrato swells in after the note starts.

• Dynamics follower: RMS rises with each attack and follows the playing. Use it to open a filter so louder notes are brighter.

name: Glass
tagline: A glass armonica: 37 tuned glass bowls you play with friction. Polyphonic, stereo, with a 12-channel output by note.

sections.panelMap:
GLASS is a physical model of a glass armonica, Benjamin Franklin's instrument of nested spinning glass bowls played with wet fingers. It has 37 bowls tuned chromatically from C3 to C6. Each bowl rings up while your finger is on it and keeps ringing after you lift it.

The display shows all 37 bowls. Ringing bowls glow in proportion to their energy.

Playing
- V/OCT (polyphonic): picks the bowls. Each channel plays the nearest bowl. With no GATE patched, V/OCT holds the bowls on.
- GATE (polyphonic): puts a finger on each bowl.
- PRESSURE (polyphonic, 0–10V): how hard each finger presses. More pressure is louder and rings up faster.
- MUTE GATE (polyphonic, matched to V/OCT): damps the matching bowl so it rings down instead of cutting off.
- DAMP ALL input and button: damps every ringing bowl.

Sliders (each with trim and CV)
- ROTATE: how fast the bowls spin, 0–6 Hz. Sets the excitation level and the speed of the wobble.
- WATER: how wet the glass is. Dry is noisy and scratchy; wet is pure and singing.
- DECAY: how long the bowls ring after you lift your finger.
- DAMP: the overall tone of all the bowls, from bright to dark.
- WOBBLE: how much the axle wobbles, adding tremolo at the rotation speed.

Lower panel
- ROOT: transposes everything, ±2 octaves.
- FM / OFFSET: pitch offset knob, plus CV with trim, applied to every bowl.
- EXT. IN and EXT. GAIN: feed audio into the bowls while they're gated.
- SPREAD: stereo width.
- VOLUME, with trim and CV.
- RMS: an envelope that follows the output level, 0–10V, with a 10-light meter.
- OUT L / R.

Poly out by note: turn it on in the context menu and OUT L, OUT R and RMS each become 12-channel poly cables, one channel per note name: channel 1 is C, channel 2 is C#, through to channel 12, which is B. Every octave of a note shares its channel, so the C3, C4, C5 and C6 bowls all come out on channel 1. SPREAD still applies, and each channel gets its own saturation and its own RMS envelope. The meter still shows the whole mix.

Context menu
- Pressure Envelope: Attack and Release for the finger pressure, and Envelope Curves (log to exponential) for each.
- Water (Grip) Noise Color: Max Noise Cutoff, how bright the noise is at the dry end of WATER.
- Poly out: one channel per note (C to B), as above.
- Damper Gate: Damper Depth, how dark a bowl goes when it's damped or muted.
- Panic: Clear All Bowl Energy.
sections.basicUse:
1. Patch a poly V/oct into V/OCT and a poly gate into GATE.
2. Set ROTATE to 1–4 Hz, the range a real player would turn the bowls.
3. Set WATER to about 0.6–0.75 for the clearest tone. Lower is scratchier; very high gets too slippery to speak.
4. Set DECAY for how long notes ring after release.
5. Shape the tone with DAMP.
6. Patch an envelope or velocity into PRESSURE for dynamics.
7. To process notes separately, turn on Poly out in the context menu and patch OUT into a poly filter, VCA or mixer.
sections.patching:
• Solo voice: One channel of V/oct and gate, an envelope into PRESSURE, WATER at 0.7, ROTATE at 2–3 Hz.

• Chords: The bowls share the available energy like a real armonica, so single notes ring louder and fuller than dense chords.

• Shaping single notes: Patch a poly gate into MUTE GATE, lined up with your V/oct channels. Muted bowls darken and fade instead of stopping dead.

• Slow blooms: A slow LFO on DAMP or WATER makes the tone open and close over time.

• Bowls as a resonator: Patch audio into EXT. IN. While gates are held, the audio excites the bowls.

• Damped rhythms: Patch a fast gate pattern into DAMP ALL with DECAY high. The bowls are cut off in rhythm against a long ring.

• Ambient clouds: DECAY high, WATER around 0.65, and short gates on a slow chord sequence. The bowls keep ringing and overlap into clouds of harmony.

• Per-note processing: Turn on Poly out and patch OUT into a poly filter or effect. Each note name has its own channel, so you can darken certain notes, delay the fifths, or pan each pitch class on its own.

• Note-name envelopes: In poly out mode RMS carries 12 envelopes, one per note name. Use them to drive a poly VCA on another voice, or to trigger something whenever a particular note rings.

name: Haze
tagline: A stereo three-voice chorus that turns into a diffuse, resonant haze as you push it.

sections.panelMap:
HAZE is a stereo chorus with three voices, each with its own feedback loop. The HAZE control takes it from a clean chorus shimmer into sustained, Doppler-drifting resonance. Each voice can also switch to a diffuse mode that smears it into something closer to a reverb.

There are six modulated delay lines, three for each side, all driven from one LFO. Left voices sit at 0°, 120° and 240°; right voices at 60°, 180° and 300°. That spacing gives natural stereo width from one control.

Nodes: the three circles at the corners of the triangle are lights and buttons, one per voice. In chorus mode a light glows blue on the positive half of its LFO and yellow on the negative half. Click it to switch that voice to diffuse mode, where it glows purple and green and the voice runs through a chain of four allpass filters. Switching fades over 3 ms, so it never clicks.

Sliders (each with trim and CV)
- RATE: LFO speed. Slow settings shimmer; fast settings give audible Doppler pitch wobble.
- DEPTH: how far the delays are modulated. The lower half is classic chorus; the upper half gets wild.
- HAZE: feedback and tone. At zero each voice dies away immediately, for a clean chorus. Turning it up feeds each delay back into itself, so the sound sustains and Doppler-shifted resonances build up. At the same time a filter in the feedback darkens the tail.

Knobs (each with trim and CV)
- DENSITY: how hard the feedback drives the saturator. Low is open and airy; high is thick and saturated.
- MIX: dry to wet.

Jacks
- IN L / R: a mono signal in L goes to both sides.
- GAIN: output level.
- OUT L / R.

Context menu
- Haze cutoff @ 0% and Haze cutoff @ 100%: the feedback filter's cutoff at each end of the HAZE slider. Set the 100% cutoff low for a dark tail, or high to keep it bright.
- Diffuse mode coefficient: how strongly the diffuse voices smear, 0.1–0.95. Default 0.7.
sections.basicUse:
1. Patch audio into IN and take OUT.

2. Start with a clean chorus:
   - RATE slow, DEPTH about a quarter, HAZE at zero, MIX at 50%.

3. Set the character:
   - DENSITY low for airy, high for thick.
   - GAIN for the output level.

4. Push into haze:
   - Raise HAZE slowly. The tails start to sustain and drift in pitch, and the tone darkens. Adjust the cutoffs in the context menu if it gets too dark or too bright.

5. Diffuse it:
   - Click a node to switch that voice to diffuse. Try one, two or all three for more smearing.

6. Modulate:
   - A slow LFO into RATE CV with the trim low gives a drifting chorus speed.
   - An envelope into HAZE CV pushes loud moments into resonance and lets quiet moments stay clean.
sections.patching:
• Classic stereo chorus: RATE slow, DEPTH a quarter, HAZE zero, MIX 50%. Widens a mono source without colouring it.

• Thick ensemble: Push DENSITY toward full for gentle saturation in the feedback.

• Shimmering tail: HAZE at 60–70%. The three voices resonate and drift with the LFO. Set the 100% cutoff below 1 kHz for a much darker tail.

• Flanger: DEPTH near the top with a very slow RATE. HAZE adds resonant peaks to the sweep.

• Diffuse cloud: All three nodes on diffuse and HAZE at 50%. The tail becomes a dense, smeared wash, good on drums and noise.

• Half and half: Put only one or two nodes in diffuse, for something between chorus and diffusion.

• Reactive fog: Patch an envelope follower into HAZE CV. Quiet passages stay clean and loud ones bloom.

• Self-oscillating resonator: HAZE at maximum and DEPTH about 20%. The voices sustain on their own and drift in pitch. Send in a short click for a pitched, ringing decay. RATE sets how fast the pitch drifts.

name: Twang
tagline: A polyphonic string you can bow, pluck, or both. With palm mute, tension twang, and a body that runs from a whistle to a cello.

sections.panelMap:
TWANG is a physical model of a single string, played with a bow, a pick, or both at once. The string is a waveguide running from nut to bridge, with a stick-slip bow at one point and a pluck at another. At the bridge it's loaded by a modelled body, so string and body work together like a real instrument instead of a string run through a filter. Up to 16 voices; the voice count follows the widest of the PITCH, PLUCK and BOW inputs, so a poly bow cable alone can play chords.

The display shows the first voice's string from nut (left) to bridge (right). The blue line with the bow is where the bow touches; the white line with the pick is where the pluck lands. The trace warms toward amber as you bow harder and add DRIVE.

Left column (knob, trim and CV)
- BOW: bow speed, -1 to +1. Zero lifts the bow; negative bows backwards. The bow takes a moment to get going and coasts to a stop. The CV is polyphonic, so each string can be bowed on its own; a mono cable bows them all.
- MUTE: palm mute. The knob (green light) sets a partial mute; the button (red light) mutes everything fully. Muting darkens the string and shortens its ring together, like a palm on the strings. The CV is polyphonic.
- TWANG: tension bend. A real string goes sharp when it's plucked hard and settles back as it rings. TWANG sets how much of that you hear.

Second column
- PITCH: knob (±2V around C4) and V/oct input, polyphonic. Notes above +2V fold down an octave to keep the bow stable.
- VOL: volume, with CV.
- FM: trim and input. The depth in semitones is set in the context menu.
- PLUCK: a trimmer for maximum pluck velocity (0–10V), a button that plucks every voice, and a trigger input. The trigger's voltage is the velocity, and harder plucks are brighter as well as louder.

Bow row (top sliders, each with trim and CV)
- BOW (blue): how much of the bow's energy reaches the string.
- BOW POS (blue): where the bow touches. Mid-string is round; near the bridge is bright and edgy.
- PRESS (blue): bow pressure. Light is airy and easy to lose; heavy is grippy and crunches at the top. The default sits at a violin-like setting.
- SLIP (blue): how fast the bow lets go once the string slips. Low is a lazy, buzzy scrape; high is crisp and articulate.
- MAT (yellow): body material, wood to metal to glass. Wood thuds, glass sings.
- TONE (red): brightness at the bridge, about 1 kHz to 18 kHz.

Pluck row (bottom sliders, each with trim and CV)
- PICK (white): pluck strength.
- PICK POS (white): where the pluck lands. Near the end is thin and twangy; mid-string is round. Polyphonic CV sets it per voice.
- DECAY (white): how long the open string rings, 0.5 s to 60 s, the same at every pitch.
- HARD (white): finger to pick. Polyphonic CV sets it per voice.
- SIZE (yellow): body size. Up is bigger: from a tiny metallic box (lowest mode around 1.2 kHz), through a guitar (131 Hz, the default), to something so big it's just thud and room (30 Hz).
- DRIVE (red): saturation after the strings, before the body, 1x to 8x.

OUT L / R (top right): stereo. The body is mono, with a subtle stereo width added around it, so it sounds like one instrument and still sums to mono cleanly.

Context menu
- Pluck: String Impedance (how hard the string resists the bow), Material Brightness Tilt (how much MAT brightens the body), Pluck Tilt.
- Body: Bridge Coupling (how much the body loads the string; 0 is a dead bridge).
- Twang: Max Bend (0–24 semitones, default 3), Twang Bounce (how far the pitch rebounds), Bounce Rate. Past 12 semitones the rebound speeds up and rings through several aftershocks.
- Pitch: FM Depth (semitones).
- Output: Poly Out (each voice on its own channel, with its own body, instead of the stereo mix), Stereo Width.
- Pickup Output: OUT L and R both carry one dry pickup on the strings, with no body, drive or stereo widening. It's what a guitar sends down the cable, ready for a fuzz or amp sim such as FUZZY.
- Pickup Position: Neck, Middle or Bridge (the default, and wound a little hotter, like a real guitar).
- Panic: Clear All Energy.
sections.basicUse:
1. Pluck it:
   - Patch a V/oct sequence into PITCH and triggers into PLUCK.
   - Gates are all 10V, so every hit is a full-strength pluck. Turn the velocity trimmer down for a gentler range, or send velocity as the trigger voltage.
   - Shape the attack with PICK POS and HARD, and the ring with DECAY.

2. Bow it:
   - Turn up BOW, or patch an envelope into the BOW CV with the trim open. The bow eases in and coasts out.
   - PRESS and SLIP set the bow's grip; BOW POS sets where it touches. If the note sputters, add pressure or speed. If it crunches, ease off.
   - A pluck lifts the bow for a moment, so you can bow and pluck the same string.

3. Choose the body:
   - SIZE for small and bright up to big and boomy, MAT for how long it rings.
   - TONE darkens the bridge; DRIVE adds grit.

4. Add expression:
   - TWANG makes hard plucks bend sharp and settle. Raise Max Bend for rubbery bends.
   - MUTE for palm-muted chugs.

5. Play chords:
   - A poly PITCH and PLUCK play one string per channel. Turn on Poly Out to pan or process each string.

TWANG sleeps when nothing is bowing or plucking and the strings have rung out.
sections.patching:
• Guitar: Poly PITCH and PLUCK from a chord sequencer, SIZE at its default, MAT low, HARD around 0.5, DECAY around 0.6, a touch of TWANG.

• Palm-muted chug: A gate pattern into MUTE CV and fast triggers into PLUCK. DRIVE up for rock.

• Cello: SIZE high, MAT low, BOW POS around 0.7, and a slow envelope on the BOW CV. Keep TONE fairly dark.

• Strum: Press PLUCK, or send one trigger on a mono cable, to pluck every voice of a held chord.

• Guitar with STRINGS: STRINGS' leftmost V/OCT into PITCH, its leftmost MUTE into the MUTE CV (trim fully up), and its TRIG into PLUCK. You get real guitar fingerings, with the strings each chord leaves out palm-muted.

• Bowed pads: A poly envelope into the BOW CV so each string swells on its own.

• Pluck over bow: Bow a quiet drone and pluck the same string on top.

• Rubber-band bass: Low notes, TWANG at full, Max Bend 12 or more, Twang Bounce around 1.

• Zither: MAT high, SIZE low, HARD high, PICK POS near the end, long DECAY.

• Spatial strings: Turn on Poly Out and patch OUT L into HOTPOT to place each string in the room.

• Fuzz guitar: Turn on Pickup Output, keep the Bridge pickup, and patch OUT L into FUZZY. TWANG is the guitar, FUZZY is the pedal.

name: Mala
tagline: A spicy stereo complex oscillator. Grafts harmonics and noise onto the crests of a sine, with a built-in LFO that moves left and right in opposite directions.

sections.panelMap:
MALA is a polyphonic stereo complex oscillator named after mala, the numbing-spicy Sichuan flavour. Oscillator A is a shaped sine. Oscillator B is an additive voice with 8 partials and an optional noise layer. HEAT drives A into a waveshaper, and wherever A's crests cross the threshold, B is grafted in. Near A's zero crossings nothing changes. So the crests take on B's harmonics while the fundamental stays solid, even at heavy settings.

The built-in LFO is the MALA bus. MA is its rate and LA its depth. It's applied in opposite directions to the left and right channels, so anything it touches moves across the stereo field.

Displays
- A (top left): the shaped sine, with the graft zones shaded.
- B (bottom left): B's waveform and its ratio to A. A band shows how much noise is in it.
- Scope (right): one cycle of the output, left and right overlaid, with the grafted parts in the heat colour.

HEAT (big knob, trim and CV): graft amount, 0–10. At zero you hear A alone.

Sliders (each with a MAP button above, trim and CV below)
- SHAPE (yellow): A's shape. Centre is a sine; left thins the crests to a point; right saturates toward a rounded square.
- RATIO (blue): B's frequency against A, 1/8x to 16x.
- MORPH (red): B's spectrum, through 20 stops: Sine, Octave, Triangle, Hollow, Square, Reed, Saw (default), Pulse 1/4, Pulse 1/8, Bright, Nasal, Vowel oo, Vowel ah, Vowel ee, Bell, Glass, Comb, Clang, Haze, Noise. The last few add noise.
- SPREAD (green): stretches B's partials from harmonic toward bell-like.
- DETUNE (white): pulls the left and right pitches apart, up to 30 cents (240 with Wide detune). It glides, and glides back into exact unison.
- PHASE (blue): moves B against A, a full cycle across the slider. Changes where B's features land on the crests.

MAP buttons: the seven buttons above HEAT and the sliders send the MALA bus to that control (lit when on). Switching fades, so it never clicks.

Mode buttons
- QUANT: snaps RATIO to 32 simple ratios between 1/8 and 16. Non-integer ratios put formants between harmonics when SYNC is on.
- SYNC (on by default): B restarts with every cycle of A, so RATIO acts like a formant.
- SYM: off grafts B onto both crests the same way (brighter, even harmonics). On makes the graft follow A's sign (hollower, odd symmetry).
SYM waits for A's next zero crossing before it switches, so it never clicks.

MALA bus
- MA: LFO rate, 0.02–50 Hz, with trim and CV.
- LA: LFO depth, with trim and polyphonic CV.

Pitch (left column)
- FM: through-zero linear FM, with a polyphonic input. At full index, 1V moves the pitch by its own frequency, and deep FM can run the oscillators backwards.
- PITCH: knob (±5V around C4) and V/oct input, polyphonic.

Outputs
- MALA, A, B: the LFO and the two raw oscillators, one channel per voice.
- VOL CV (0–10V VCA, polyphonic) and VOL knob.
- OUTS: L and R.

Context menu
- Supersampling: 2x, 4x, 8x, or Auto (default). Auto picks the lowest setting that keeps the current pitch and HEAT clean.
- Polyphonic outputs (default on): L and R carry one channel per voice. Off mixes them down.
- Wide detune (240 cents).
- B brightness: a gentle rolloff on B's partials, 800 Hz to 20 kHz (default 3.5 kHz).
- Texture seed (0–31): changes the noise's waveform, not its spectrum or level.
- Mala wave: Sine (default), Triangle or Slow random.
- Ma CV overrides Mala (depth by La): while the MA CV jack is patched, your CV replaces the internal LFO, scaled by LA.
- Mala voice phase: Spread (default), where each voice's LFO is offset so chords shimmer, or Unison.
sections.basicUse:
1. Start with A:
   - Patch V/oct into PITCH. With HEAT at zero you hear the shaped sine. Move SHAPE to thin or round it.

2. Graft B:
   - Turn up HEAT slowly. B's harmonics bloom on the crests while the fundamental holds.
   - Choose B's spectrum with MORPH and its ratio with RATIO. With SYNC on, sweeping RATIO moves a formant.
   - Press QUANT to lock RATIO to clean intervals. Toggle SYM to hear bright against hollow.

3. Widen it:
   - DETUNE for a chorused split, PHASE to move B on the crests, SPREAD for metal.

4. Animate it:
   - Light one or more MAP buttons and raise LA. MA sets the speed. Even one destination moves in stereo.

5. Play it:
   - The outputs are polyphonic by default, so patch them into a poly VCA or mixer, or use the VOL CV as a built-in VCA.
sections.patching:
• Spicy bass: Low notes, SHAPE a little right, MORPH on Saw, RATIO 2x with QUANT, HEAT around 4. An envelope on HEAT gives a filter-like bite that keeps the fundamental.

• Talking lead: MORPH on the vowels with SYNC on. Sweep MORPH and RATIO for vowel and formant movement.

• Stereo shimmer pad: A poly chord into PITCH, DETUNE up, MAP on PHASE and SPREAD, MA slow, LA moderate.

• Bells and gongs: SPREAD high, MORPH on Bell or Glass, SYNC off, a non-integer RATIO, and a percussive envelope on VOL CV.

• Breathy tone: MORPH toward Haze or Noise with HEAT low. The noise only appears on the crests, so it sounds like breath riding the note.

• Through-zero FM: Patch another oscillator into FM. HEAT adds its harmonics on top of the FM sidebands.

• External bus: Turn on Ma CV overrides Mala and patch a sequencer or envelope into MA. The MAP buttons and the stereo movement now follow your modulation.

name: HotPot
tagline: A spatial mixer for up to 96 sources. Place and move them around the listener, in a shared room, through a tube-warmed bus.

sections.panelMap:
HOTPOT is a three-track polyphonic spatial mixer, with controls named after a hot pot dinner. Every input channel is a source placed around a virtual listener. Each source gets real distance and direction cues: level, timing between the ears, head shadow, air absorption, front and back colouring, and Doppler when it moves. All sources share one diffuse room, and the mix runs through a saturating stereo bus. Each track has two poly inputs, so a track holds up to 32 sources and the whole pot up to 96.

The tracks
- STIR (cyan): a ring around the listener, 4 m away at 1x. Position is the angle, ±180°.
- SHABU (chili): a stage 6 m in front, ±12 m left to right.
- FAN (yellow): two tracks, one each side, running from narrow behind you to wide in front. IN A goes to the left track and IN B to the right (if only A is patched, its channels alternate sides). Position runs back to front.

The pot (top centre) is a map seen from above, front at the top. Each source is a dot in its track's colour, sized by its level. SKIM sits in the middle, where the listener is: press it and every source glides home, the light stays on while they settle, and motion starts again from the beginning.

Track strips (one per track)
- ↔ button: motion mode, Parallel (the default) or Mirrored, lit in the track colour when mirrored.
  - Stir: parallel turns everything together; mirrored turns the two halves opposite ways.
  - Shabu: parallel swishes the group side to side; mirrored opens and closes the two halves.
  - Fan: parallel moves both tracks front and back together; mirrored rocks them against each other.
- M button: mute, with a fade. The room tail rings out naturally.
- ANGLE (Stir) or POS slider: home position. Polyphonic CV positions each source.
- SPREAD slider: how far apart the sources sit.
- LEVEL slider: track level, unity at three-quarters. The CV is a 0–10V VCA, normalled to 10V; polyphonic CV sets each source.
- RATE knob: motion speed, 0.01 Hz up to 7 Hz, off at the bottom. The top of the range is fast enough for rotating-speaker effects.
- IN A and IN B (polyphonic).
Moving sources keep their order and spacing, and close up near the end of a track instead of folding back.

Room and scene (knob, trim and CV)
- BROTH: room send, 25% by default.
- MSG: room decay.
- STEAM: diffusion first, then slow modulation of the room above about 20%.
- LID: the room's damping, 1 kHz to 20 kHz.
- POT: scene size, 0.25x to 10x. Scales every distance and the room together.
- SPICE: cue strength, 0–300%. 100% is natural. Above that the cues get more vivid: far sources wetter, near ones drier, ears further apart. The CV covers the full range over 10V.

Main
- M button: main mute.
- SIMMER slider, trim and CV: the lower half is volume; the upper half drives a tube stage (up to +20 dB) for warm, even-harmonic saturation.
- OUTS: L and R.

Headroom is automatic. Each track shares out the level of its active channels, a gentle leveler keeps a full pot under control, and a soft clip catches rare peaks below 10.5V. On load the output fades in over about two seconds. Bypassed, the A inputs go left and the B inputs right.

Context menu
- Motion shape: Sine, Triangle or Stepped (8 steps per cycle with short glides), for each track.
- Haas far-ear delay: how far the far ear lags. Natural (default), Wide, Wider or Widest (60 ms) for an exaggerated stereo spread.
- Doppler: pitch shift from moving sources, kept to a few cents. On by default.
- Full-bandwidth room (more CPU): runs the room at the full sample rate instead of half.
sections.basicUse:
1. Fill the pot:
   - Patch poly voices into a track's IN A. Each channel is a source and appears as a dot.
   - STIR for sounds all around, SHABU for a band in front, FAN for sounds coming from behind.

2. Place them:
   - ANGLE / POS sets where the group sits; SPREAD sets how far apart.
   - LEVEL sets the track level. Patch envelopes into the LEVEL CV for a VCA on each source.

3. Set the room:
   - BROTH sets how much goes into the room; MSG how long it rings.
   - LID darkens it; STEAM thickens it and, higher up, sets it gently moving.
   - POT scales the whole scene from a small room to a hall.

4. Make it move:
   - Turn up RATE on a track. Try both settings of the ↔ button.
   - Pick Sine, Triangle or Stepped motion in the context menu.
   - Press SKIM to bring everything home.

5. Season to taste:
   - SPICE above 100% for a more vivid space, below for something closer to a plain panner.
   - SIMMER past halfway warms the whole mix.

HOTPOT is made for headphones and stereo speakers. Directional cues come across best on headphones.
sections.patching:
• Surround chord: A poly chord into STIR IN A, SPREAD full, RATE slow, ↔ on Mirrored. The notes orbit you, half one way and half the other.

• Band on a stage: Drums into SHABU IN A, bass and keys into SHABU IN B, SPREAD around 0.5, BROTH 20–30%.

• Fly-by: One source on FAN with Triangle motion and RATE moderate. It sweeps from behind to in front, with Doppler and air absorption.

• Notes in their own places: Poly random or sequence CV into STIR's ANGLE CV puts every note of a chord at its own angle.

• Spatial VCA: Poly envelopes into LEVEL CV. Each source is gated on its own while sharing the room.

• Rotating speaker: An organ or pad alone on STIR, SPREAD at zero, RATE near the top (6–7 Hz). It spins around your head like a fast Leslie, with Doppler and head shadow doing the work.

• Hopping sources: Stepped motion on SHABU with RATE low. The sources jump between eight places with short glides.

• Vivid space: SPICE at 200%, POT large, BROTH 40%. Distant sources sink into the room while near ones stay close and dry.

• Warm bus: SIMMER three-quarters up, with a slow LFO on its CV for breathing saturation.

• Spatial strings: TWANG with Poly Out on, into STIR IN A, so each string has its own place.

name: Fuzzy
tagline: Eight classic fuzz and overdrive pedals simulated from their schematics, with a guitar volume knob for clean-up and a battery that drains until the circuit sputters out.

sections.panelMap:
FUZZY is a fuzz pedal with eight circuits inside, each one simulated from the original schematic, transistor by transistor. The input is levelled so whatever you patch in arrives like a hot single-coil pickup, so synths, drums and samples all hit the circuit the way a guitar would.

Display
- The model's name and its circuit: how many transistors, germanium or silicon, and the topology.
- A glyph for each transistor and diode, which glows with the current through it and changes colour when it saturates.
- A level meter on the left and a battery icon on the right.

Models
- ROUNDHOUSE: after the Arbiter Fuzz Face (UK, 1966). Two germanium PNP transistors with shunt feedback.
- RASP: after the Sola Sound Tone Bender MK1 (UK, 1965). Three germanium PNPs: a follower and two gain stages.
- SUSTAINER: after the Tone Bender MK2 (UK, 1966). Three germanium PNPs: a boost into a feedback pair.
- SPLUTTER: after the Vox/JEN Tone Bender (Italy, 1966). Two germanium PNPs, with Q2 biased near cutoff.
- BUZZSAW: after the Maestro FZ-1 Fuzz-Tone (US, 1962). Three germanium PNPs on a 3V cell.
- KAIJU: after the Univox Super-Fuzz (Japan, 1968), the scooped octave fuzz. Five silicon NPNs and two germanium diodes.
- HORNET: after the Ibanez Standard Fuzz (Japan, 1970s), a flatter octave fuzz. A JFET, three silicon transistors and a germanium diode.
- KALEIDO: after the Colorsound Power Boost (UK, 1970). Three silicon NPNs, an 18V feedback pair and EQ.
Each model is level-matched, so switching between them changes the character, not the loudness.

Controls
- BATT: the battery's charge, 0–100%. Turn it down and the supply sags and the junctions warm up, until the circuit sputters and dies. With trim and CV.
- FUZZ: each circuit's gain or bias pot, mapped over its sweet spot. With trim and CV.
- GUITAR: the guitar's volume knob, in front of the circuit. Rolling it back cleans up the fuzz the way it does on a real guitar, and the taper spreads the clean-up across the whole knob. With trim and CV.
- MODEL: picks the circuit. The CV is 1V per model and wraps around. Changes crossfade and are rate-limited, so CV can't switch models at audio rate.
- VOL: output volume. The CV covers the full range at 10V.
- SWITCH: the footswitch. The button or a trigger at the jack toggles the pedal, and the red light shows it's on. It fades between the circuit and the clean, levelled input.
- IN and OUT: mono. The output has a DC blocker and a soft limiter.

Context menu
- Oversampling: Off (1x), 2x, 4x (the default) or 8x.
sections.basicUse:
1. Patch a sound into IN and take OUT to your mixer.
2. Pick a MODEL. ROUNDHOUSE is a good place to start.
3. Set FUZZ for the amount of grind.
4. Roll GUITAR back to clean it up, and back up for the full fuzz.
5. Turn BATT down for a dying-battery sputter.
sections.patching:
• Guitar rig: TWANG with Pickup Output on (Bridge pickup) into IN. TWANG is the guitar and FUZZY is the pedal.

• Swell into fuzz: An envelope or a slow LFO into GUITAR's CV, so notes bloom from clean into fuzz like a player riding the volume knob.

• Gated sputter: A random LFO on BATT's CV. The pedal chokes and recovers on its own.

• Pedal-board switching: A sequencer's gates into SWITCH to kick the fuzz in on certain bars.

• Model sequencing: A stepped sequence into MODEL CV changes circuits each bar, with crossfades between them.

• Octave fuzz on synths: KAIJU or HORNET on a simple saw or square bass for the octave-up ring.

name: Vega
tagline: Bass pedals after a classic 1976 analog bass-pedal synthesizer: two saws into a transistor ladder, with the original presets and a programmable VARIABLE console.

sections.panelMap:
VEGA is a bass-pedal synth after a classic 1976 design, simulated from the schematic and service bulletin: two sawtooth oscillators into a transistor ladder filter, contour generators for the filter and the VCA, and the pitch hold that keeps the note sounding after you lift your foot. It's polyphonic up to 16 voices, and each voice gets its own part tolerances.

Top row
- PITCH and GATE inputs: V/oct and gate, mono or poly. A patched GATE plays whatever PITCH holds.
- GRIT: how hard the circuit is driven, 1/4x to 4x around noon, with makeup gain. With trim and CV.
- SNARL: in the bottom half, osc B's saw swings the cutoff (±4 octaves at half travel). From 0.4 up it crossfades in a sub-octave that also frequency-modulates osc A, and the note growls an octave down. With trim and CV.
- GATE and PITCH outputs: the gate and the held pitch for each voice, so the pedals can play other modules too.

Left column
- TUNE: ±1.5 semitones, both oscillators.
- BEAT: detunes osc B, ±34 cents.
- GLIDE: glide time, 5 ms to 1 s, when the GLIDE switch is on.
Each has a CV jack. TUNE and BEAT CVs add a fifth of the knob's range per volt.

VARIABLE PRESET SETTING
This is the programmable preset, played when VAR is selected. The sliders light up while any voice is on VARIABLE. Each slider has a CV input, worth 10% of its travel per volt.
- OCT: the Variable preset's octave, Lo, Med or Hi.
- B–A: the oscillator mix, all B at the bottom and all A at the top.
- OSC B: osc B's interval, −1 to +13 semitones.
- VOLUME ATTACK, SUS and DECAY: the volume contour.
- CUTOFF: 0–4 octaves above the base cutoff.
- EMPH: emphasis (resonance), 0–10. It self-oscillates from about 8.
- AMT: how much the filter contour moves the cutoff.
- FILTER ATTACK and DECAY: the filter contour.

Presets and switches
- MODE: preset CV, 1V per preset, wrapping every 4V. A poly CV gives each voice its own preset.
- VAR, VEGA, TUBA, BASS: the presets. VEGA, TUBA and BASS use the values from the original preset switches. VEGA is the default.
- GLIDE: on uses the GLIDE knob's time; off, notes change almost instantly.
- DECAY: on by default. Off gives a fast release.
- OCTAVE: low or high. Switching glides between them.

Bottom
- VOLUME: the volume foot pedal, with trim and CV.
- FILTER: the filter foot pedal, 42.9 Hz to 3 kHz, with trim and CV. The cutoff also tracks the keyboard.
- AUX: an external input into the mixer, ahead of the filter. The button above it chooses Mix (alongside the oscillators) or Filter only, where the oscillators drop out and the VCA stays open, following the VOLUME pedal.
- Pedals: 13 clickable pedals, C to C. Drag across them to slide legato. The mouse plays voice 0.
- OUT: audio.

In release, the held pitch droops 12 cents per second, as on the original.

Context menu
- Oversampling: Off, 2x (the default) or 4x.
- OUT: Polyphonic, a channel per voice (the default), or Summed to mono.
- Voice variation: each voice gets its own part tolerances. On by default.
- V/Oct range: Folded onto the pedals, C1 to C2 (the default), so any pitch lands on the 13 pedals, or Full range.
sections.basicUse:
1. Click the pedals to play. Drag across them for legato.
2. Try the VEGA, TUBA and BASS presets.
3. Pick VAR and shape your own sound with the sliders.
4. Ride the FILTER and VOLUME pedals.
5. For a sequence, patch V/oct into PITCH and gates into GATE.
sections.patching:
• Bass from a sequencer: Patch a sequence into PITCH and GATE. With V/Oct range folded, every note lands on the pedals, an octave from C1 to C2.

• Wah pedal: An envelope or slow LFO into FILTER's CV.

• Poly drones: A poly chord into PITCH and GATE with OUT left polyphonic, then into HOTPOT to spread the voices around the room.

• Preset sequencing: A stepped CV into MODE changes preset each step. With poly CV, each voice can play a different preset.

• Filter an outside sound: Set AUX to Filter only and patch a drum loop or pad into AUX. VEGA becomes a ladder filter, played with the FILTER and VOLUME pedals.

• Growl: SNARL past 0.4 with GRIT up for the sub-octave snarl.

• Pedals as a controller: The GATE and PITCH outputs carry what you play, so the pedals can drive another voice in unison.

name: Syzygy
tagline: Two stereo phase-feedback oscillators that cross over: ring mod, AM, cross-FM, folding and noise. From glass bells to metallic chaos.

sections.panelMap:
SYZYGY is a complex oscillator made of two stereo phase-feedback oscillators that can ring-modulate, amplitude-modulate and cross-FM each other. It's inspired by chromosomal crossover: the two oscillators recombine, and on the display their product bridges the two centres like a pair of chromosomes. It covers everything from bell and glass-like ring modulation to the metallic clang of linear through-zero cross-FM.

Oscillators I and II (each)
- V/OCT knob and input. A polyphonic V/OCT turns on polyphony for the whole module and every CV input.
- FM knob and input: linear FM, added to V/OCT. The FM inputs are normalled so each oscillator modulates the other; patching a cable breaks the normal. Exponential FM and depth options are in the context menu.
- LOCK: hard-syncs this oscillator to the other one.
- SYNC input: hard-syncs on a rising zero crossing.
- LFO button (oscillator II): LFO mode, where 0V is 1 Hz.

Harmonic palette (sliders for each oscillator, each with an attenuverter and CV)
- FEEDBACK: amount of phase feedback. At zero you get a sine, and POS, NODE and RATIO do nothing.
- POS: where in the cycle the feedback lands, ±360°.
- NODE: number of nodes in the feedback phase. Oscillator I runs 0–5. Oscillator II runs -3.5 to 3.5 with a symmetric pattern, which gives it a different but related sound to OUROS.
- PHASE: the oscillator's base phase, ±360°. After ALIGN, use it to set the two oscillators against each other.
- SPREAD: offsets left and right from PHASE. Your ears hear the two sides at slightly different times, which gives a spatial effect.
- RATIO: frequency of the feedback, 1–10x. Like an FM operator ratio, it sounds best at whole numbers, and the slider is mapped to spend most of its travel near them.

[[fig:node-i]]

[[fig:node-ii]]

Display
- The left (orange) and right (blue) channels of each oscillator, drawn as one cycle in polar form. The cross-modulation product bridges the two centres.
- CHAN: which poly channel to show. Above the poly count, it shows the last one.
- ALIGN: pulses both SYNC inputs at once, realigning the two oscillators.

Mixer (sliders, each with an attenuverter and CV)
- MOD/MIX: from a plain mix of I and II to the cross-modulated sound.
- XFM: cross-FM amount. Which oscillator it modulates is set in the context menu.
- RING/AM: ring modulation to AM. In AM you hear the carrier; in ring modulation only the sidebands. The difference can be subtle, but it's lovely when the oscillators are tuned to an interval.
- SYM: DC offset before the wavefolder.
- FOLD: wavefolding. At the top it turns into saturation.
- PINK/WHITE: noise colour.
- NOISE/CLEAN: from the clean signal to noise.

Outputs
- I OUT and II OUT: stereo outputs for each oscillator.
- MAIN OUT: the stereo mix.
- VOLUME, with attenuverter and CV: a VCA on the outputs.

Context menu
- FM Range: maximum FM depth.
- FM Mode: Linear TZFM or Exponential V/Oct.
- XFM Mode: cross-modulate oscillator I (the usual complex-oscillator routing, and the default), II, or both.
- 2x Supersampling on Ring/AM Mixer: cleaner cross-modulation at more CPU.
- Mix Down Main Outputs: sums the poly outputs to one channel.
- Volume VCA also controls OscI and OscII outs: on by default. Turn it off for full-level I and II outputs.

Technical notes

How does phase-feedback distortion work? The oscillator's phase isn't fixed. A portion of another oscillator's output is fed back to push it around, like the ouroboros eating its own tail. Each cycle the phase lands a little off its ideal position, so the waveform bends and skews. The more feedback, the more distortion.

[[fig:feedback]]

The RATIO mapping: RATIO scales the phase oscillator against the main one, much like an FM ratio, and whole numbers sound best. The slider is mapped through steep 5th-order curves so it still covers the whole range but spends most of its travel near whole numbers.

[[fig:ratio]]
sections.basicUse:
1. Set the pitch:
   - Patch V/oct into oscillator I, II or both.

2. Choose the relationship:
   - Let the oscillators run free, or press LOCK to sync one to the other. Press ALIGN to snap them back into phase.

3. Build the harmonics:
   - FEEDBACK sets how much phase distortion. NODE, POS and RATIO shape it. SPREAD widens it.

4. Mix:
   - MOD/MIX from a plain mix to cross-modulation, RING/AM between the two, and XFM for cross-FM. The FM inputs already cross-modulate until you patch them.

5. Add texture:
   - FOLD for wavefolding, SYM to make it asymmetric, NOISE/CLEAN for noise.

6. Make it a voice:
   - VOLUME is up by default, so SYZYGY works as an oscillator. Set it to 0 and patch an envelope into VOLUME and it becomes a complete polyphonic synth voice.
sections.patching:
• Plucks from a drone: Set up a drone with moderate FEEDBACK and NODE, then send an envelope to FOLD. Each hit gives a short burst of folded harmonics.

• Bells and glass: Tune the oscillators to an interval and morph RING/AM.

• Cross-FM motion: Leave the FM normals in and sweep XFM.

• Wild drums and effects: Set XFM Mode to Both and push XFM for screaming or bubbling sounds. Great for sculpting percussion.

• Stereo snap: Set SPREAD moderately wide and press ALIGN at the start of each phrase.

• Noise layers: Morph in pink or white noise for landscapes or to give drums some grit.

• Poly voice: Poly V/oct into oscillator I, VOLUME at 0, a poly envelope into VOLUME. Route the envelope to FOLD too, for brighter attacks.

figures.caption: Oscillator I: how NODE 0–5 maps the phase feedback onto the oscillator.
Oscillator II: a symmetric node pattern from -3.5 to 3.5.
Phase-feedback distortion with RATIO = 2: the feedback oscillator, the distorted oscillator and a reference sine.
The RATIO mapping. Most of the slider's travel sits close to whole numbers.

name: Super Wonk
tagline: Sixteen LFOs locked to your clock. Wonk them out of phase, then ALIGN them back together.

sections.panelMap:
SUPER WONK is a 16-channel LFO with phase-feedback distortion. It morphs sixteen synchronized oscillators into more chaotic shapes that still stay locked to the clock. Its ALIGN input pulls all sixteen into line and lets them go again.

Clock
- CLOCK: syncs the LFOs to an external clock. Without one they run at 30 BPM.
- RESET: back to the default phases set by NODES. Also has a button.
- RATE X: multiplies the clock with positive values, divides it with negative values, from -24 to +24. Between -1 and 1 it runs at 1x. Has an attenuverter and CV.

Shaping (each with an attenuverter and CV)
- PHASE: a phase offset for all sixteen. Use it for fine timing, or modulate it for much more complex outputs.
- MOD DEPTH: output level, up to 5V.
- WONK: amount of phase feedback. Any WONK makes the oscillators drift slowly out of phase while staying centred on the beat. As WONK rises, the range of NODES narrows and the outputs morph from unison into chaos.
- FDBK POS: which channel the feedback comes from, 1–16. Each gives the wonk a slightly different feel.
- NODES: phase spacing between the channels, -8 to +8.
  - 0: all in unison.
  - 1: evenly spaced, rotating clockwise. Negative values rotate the other way.
  - 2: the phases go round 720°, so each output appears twice.
  - 8: four full rotations, four of each output, in an even/odd pattern.

ALIGN: a gate here (or the button) makes all sixteen fade into alignment, over 2 seconds by default. When the gate goes low they fade back to their NODES positions.

[[fig:align]]

Outputs
- 1–16: the sixteen LFOs. The display shows each one's value.
- P: all sixteen as one poly cable.

Context menu
- Align fade time: up to 16 seconds.
- Output polyphony: each output can carry a group of channels, wrapping back to 1 after 16.
- Unipolar mode (0-10V): outputs 0–10V instead of ±5V. MOD DEPTH and the display follow.
sections.basicUse:
1. Patch a clock into CLOCK.
2. Set RATE X for the speed against the clock.
3. Set NODES to spread the sixteen channels in phase.
4. Raise WONK to let them drift and bend while staying on the beat.
5. Send a gate into ALIGN to pull them together, and release it to let them spread out again.
sections.patching:
• Sixteen-lane mod bus: Patch neighbouring outputs to related parameters (filter cutoffs, pans, wavefolders) for motion that feels connected.

• Phase collapse: Moderate WONK, and a gate into ALIGN every 4 or 8 bars. Everything sweeps into unison and back.

• Rotating wheel: NODES at 1 and a slow RATE X. The sixteen channels turn like a modulation wheel.

• Poly groups: Set Output polyphony so each jack carries a group of channels for poly voices.

figures.caption: ALIGN: on a rising gate the channels fade into alignment; on a falling gate they fade back to their NODES positions. Shown at three WONK settings.

name: Envelope City
tagline: Sixteen related envelopes. Set the first and last, and fourteen more fill in between.

sections.panelMap:
ENVELOPE CITY is ENVELOPE ARRAY grown into a city: sixteen envelopes that belong together. Set the width, slant and curve of the first and the last; the fourteen in between fill in. Each channel has its own trigger, button and end-of-cycle gate, so it's built for self-patching, and it can run itself as an oscillator.

FIRST (left) and LAST (right), each with attenuverter and CV
- WIDTH: cycle time of channel 1 (FIRST) or channel 16 (LAST), in seconds.
- SLANT: from a rising ramp, through a pyramid, to a falling ramp.
- CURVE: from log to linear to exponential.
- RETRIG: one button for channels 1–8 and one for 9–16. On, an envelope can be retriggered while it falls. Off, a trigger waits for the envelope to finish.

INTERPOLATED ENVELOPES (centre slider): skews how the in-between channels are distributed between FIRST and LAST.

[[fig:shapes]]

Channels (16)
- INPUTS: a trigger input for each channel. Each is normalled to the next, so one trigger into input 1 fires them all.
- BUTTONS: trigger each channel by hand.
- ENVELOPES: sixteen outputs.
- GATES: go high while their envelope is at 0V. Use them to chain and loop.
- POLY: poly outputs for the envelopes and for the gates.
The display colours match the colours of the cables you patch.

Context menu
- Output Polyphony Settings: how many channels each envelope output and each gate output carries. The groups wrap back to 1 after 16.
- Trigger Probability: a chance for each channel to fire, set per channel (Channels 1–8 and 9–16 submenus) or for all at once.
- Volcano-shaped Envelopes: by default CURVE flips at the peak, giving shark-fin shapes. Volcano mode applies it the same way on both sides.

[[fig:volcano]]
sections.basicUse:
1. Set FIRST and LAST WIDTH. The fourteen in between take the times between them.
2. Shape FIRST and LAST with SLANT and CURVE. Giving the two ends different shapes makes a fan of related envelopes that peak at different times.
3. Patch one trigger into input 1 to fire them all, or separate triggers for separate timing.
4. Patch the GATES back into the inputs to chain and loop.
5. Use RETRIG and Trigger Probability to control how they respond.
sections.patching:
• Velocity fan: Send the sixteen envelopes to sixteen VCAs for a spread from fast to slow across voices.

• Chains: Patch GATE N into input N+1 to build long chains of envelopes without a clock.

• LFOs: With short widths, patch a GATE back into its own input. The envelope cycles on its own.

• Random fills: Turn on Trigger Probability and set some channels to 60–80% for drum patterns that vary from one trigger.

• Mallets: Turn on Volcano-shaped Envelopes for rounded shapes that feel like plucks or mallets.

figures.caption: Different CURVE and SLANT settings for FIRST and LAST give families of related envelopes that peak at different times.
Shark-fin envelopes (default, left) and volcano envelopes (right).

name: Arrange XL
tagline: ARRANGE with sixteen channels, built-in editing buttons, and room for whole compositions.

sections.panelMap:
ARRANGE XL is a sixteen-channel step sequencer. Each channel can record its input, quantize to semitones, or fire probability triggers, and the copy, paste and edit buttons are right on the panel.

Transport
- STAGE: selects the stage.
- END: sequence length, up to 128 stages (up to 2048 in the context menu). Changing it resets to the start and rescales STAGE.
- REC: arms recording, with a button and input. The light turns red.
- EDIT: with EDIT off, stages are overwritten as you move through them while recording. With EDIT on, each stage's values are loaded onto the knobs so you can change them.
- BACK / FWD: step backwards or forwards, with buttons and inputs. Clock FWD to play.
- RESET: back to stage 1.

Display: the top shows the stage and length, with a white dot for progress. The column shows each channel's voltage, note or probability.

Channels (16)
- IN: overrides the knob. A poly input spreads downward across the channels.
- MODE button: Voltage (off), semitone quantizer (blue), or probability triggers (yellow). In probability mode -10V is 0% and +10V is 100%.
- Knob and OUT.
- P: poly output.

Editing buttons
- COPY: copies the current stage. COPY ALL copies every stage up to the current one. Their lights show the copy buffer is full.
- PASTE: inserts the copied stages after the current one. The stages after it move back to make room.
- ROTATE: makes the current stage stage 1. The stages before it wrap around to the end.
- CLEAR: resets the current stage.
- ADD / DELETE: inserts or removes a stage, changing the length by one.
- Shift-click a knob while recording to apply its value to every stage.

Context menu
- Individual Output Polyphony: how many channels each output carries, wrapping after 16.
- Set Max Sequence Length: 128, 256, 512, 1024 or 2048.
- Stop Record At End: REC turns off when the sequence loops, so you capture exactly one pass.
- Clone Copied Stage to All: copies the first copied stage over every stage.
- Rotate Sequence to Start Here: the same as ROTATE.
sections.basicUse:
1. Set END.
2. Clock FWD.
3. Choose a MODE for each channel.
4. Step through with REC on and set the knobs, or patch CV into IN and record as it plays.
5. Use the editing buttons to build longer arrangements from the stages you've made.
sections.patching:
• A whole track: Set some channels to semitones for melody and bass, others to probability for drums, and use the rest for mixer and effect CVs.

• Live recording: Patch a controller into IN with REC on, and turn on Stop Record At End to catch one loop.

• Arranging: Copy a section, paste it after itself, and edit the copies into variations.

• Changing lengths: Use ADD and DELETE while it plays for unexpected changes of length.
