name: Chord Caster
tagline: A whole composition in one module: chord sequencer, rhythm section, six-voice stereo oscillator, modulation, mixer and delay.

sections.panelMap:
CHORD CASTER lets you write and sequence complete pieces in VCV Rack. It has a chord quantizer with 192 hand-programmed guitar-style voicings (each of the 16 chord types has its own voicing for every note of the scale), a six-voice stereo oscillator based on OUROS, a rhythm section, a tempo-synced modulation bus, compression and tanh saturation, and a three-tap delay. Every knob can be recorded per stage, so one module can play a whole song.

The panel is laid out in 16 areas, numbered in the two pictures below.

[[fig:overview-a]]

1. Recorder: RECORD turns recording on and off. NOTES, BEATS and KNOBS choose what gets recorded, and the red light means something is recording. When the STAGE moves on, the recorded settings are written to the stage you're leaving.
   - NOTES (red): the chord, root and each voice's NOTE offset. CV SLEW glides the notes between stages.
   - BEATS (green): the beat ratios, STRUM, RETRIG ENV, CLOCK and BEATS.
   - KNOBS (blue): every knob and attenuverter. KNOB SLEW glides them between stages.
   - EDIT: off by default, so stages are overwritten as you move through them. With EDIT on, moving to a stage loads its settings so you can change them, and moving on saves them.

2. Clock: CLOCK sets the tempo in BPM. BEATS sets how many clock pulses each stage lasts (1–99). When a clock is patched into CLOCK TRIG., the knob follows it.

3. Transport: PLAY starts the sequence (blue). Shift-click PLAY to loop the current stage (yellow), which is handy for auditioning. RESET goes back to stage 1; REV and FWD move one stage. Each has an input.

4. Chord sequencer: STAGE picks the current stage and MAX sets how many there are. The display shows stage/max and the chord. Pick the root on the keyboard (the − and + buttons change octave) and the chord type with the 16 buttons: M, m, 7, M7, m7, 6, m6, 9, M9, m9, +9, sus2, sus4, 5, aug, dim. A mono V/OCT input sets the root. A poly V/OCT input replaces the chord, filling the six voices with its notes (copied as needed).

5. Notes: shows the note on each of the six voices, with a scope of each voice's waveform. NOTE − and + move single voices up or down. Changing the root keeps your changes; choosing a new chord type resets them. With a poly V/OCT patched, the chord buttons are disabled and the NOTE offsets still work.

6. Beat programmer: X and 1/Y set a clock ratio for each voice, like a simple SYNCRO without rotation, swing or width. X at 0 silences that voice. The beats are stored per stage, so the rhythm can change with the sequence.

7. Envelopes: like ENVELOPE ARRAY. WIDTH I sets voice 1's envelope length and WIDTH VI voice 6's, with the rest in between. SLANT and CURVE shape them. The beat programmer's gates trigger them, the display shows each one live, and a LEVEL trimpot per voice sets its depth.

[[fig:overview-b]]

8. Modulation: a six-channel modulation bus related to HEX MOD.
   - RATE x: cycles per stage. 1 is one cycle per stage; -2 is one cycle every two stages, down to -16. Between -1 and 1 it stays at 1, a wide landing pad for resyncing while you play.
   - NODES: how the six channels are spread in phase, -3 to +3. 0 is unison; ±1 spaces them 60° apart (positive turns clockwise, negative anticlockwise); ±2 spaces them 120° apart, two copies of three; ±3 spaces them 180° apart, three copies of two opposed pairs.
   - WONK: self-modulation of RATE and NODES, taken from the channel set by POS.
   - MOD. DEPTH: depth for all six channels.
   The bus restarts whenever a new note comes in, so repeated stages of the same chord play as a tie. With WONK past 0.5 the modulators run free.

9. Oscillator: a six-voice stereo OUROS. SPREAD, OFFSET (with FM), FEEDBACK, PHASE, POS, MULTI and NODE work as on OUROS, each with an attenuverter fed by the modulation bus. The circular display shows the top voice in stereo.

10. Mix: STEREO SPREAD pans the six voices from right-to-left through to left-to-right (it also sets the delay tap pans). PRESS compresses and saturates like PRESSED DUCK, with lights for the compression. GAIN sets the level into the delay; above 1 it drives the feedback harder, and its light shows distortion.

11. Delay FX: a small TRI DELAY with smooth fractional delay lines.
   - DELAY: master delay time, up to 36, 360 or 3600 ms depending on BUFFER SIZE.
   - REVERB: feedback. With the 36 ms buffer, high REVERB gives Karplus-Strong plucks.
   - TAPS I, II, III: offsets from DELAY.
   - CENTER: how the feedback is shared between the taps.
   - DRY/WET and VOLUME.
   The scope shows the dry envelope in orange and the wet in blue. The three dots are the taps: position is time, size is feedback, colour is pan.

12. STRUM and RETRIG ENV.: STRUM lets the modulation bus trigger the envelopes instead of the beats, for strum patterns that follow the stages. RETRIG ENV. lets envelopes retrigger before they finish.

13. Copy and paste: COPY, PASTE, CLEAR, ADD and DELETE work on the current stage. Shift-click COPY to copy every stage up to the current one. The COPY light is blue for one stage and yellow for several.

14. Slew: CV SLEW and KNOB SLEW glide notes and knobs between stages while playing (not while recording), up to the length of the stage.

15. Inputs: CLOCK TRIG. (tempo from the last two pulses), V/OCT, CHORD, EXT., FEEDBACK, WONK, MOD. DEPTH, PRESS, DRY/WET and VOLUME. Inputs override the panel. EXT. depends on the context menu.

16. Outputs: NOTES, GATES, ENVS and MODS are six-channel poly outputs from their sections. STAGE sends a trigger on each stage change. AUDIO OUT L and R are the stereo mix.

Shift-click any knob while recording KNOBS to apply it to every stage. This works on STRUM and RETRIG ENV. too.

Context menu
- Set Max Sequence Length: the range of MAX, up to 2048. CHORD CASTER always remembers all 2048 stages, so shortening and lengthening again brings back what was there.
- Stop Record At End: stops recording when the sequence loops, so you don't record over the start.
- External Input Mode: what EXT. does.
  - Maps to VCA: replaces the internal oscillator with an external poly signal (channels 1–6 left, 7–12 right).
  - Triggers Envelopes: a poly gate triggers envelopes 1–6 directly.
  - Maps to Modulation: replaces the modulation bus. Fewer than six channels are copied up to six.
  - Maps to V/Oct Offset: adds to each voice's pitch. A mono signal transposes all six, so another sequencer can transpose the whole piece.
- Stage outputs main clock instead of stage clock.
- Sync modulation bus to main clock instead of stage clock.
- Output dry poly audio: AUDIO OUT carries the six dry oscillator voices, and the mixer and delay are switched off.
- Save CPU: on by default. Turn it off for 8x supersampling and smoother envelopes.
sections.basicUse:
1. Choose a chord: click a root on the keyboard and a chord type.
2. Set a rhythm: give each voice a ratio with X and 1/Y.
3. Shape the sound: envelopes with WIDTH, SLANT and CURVE; the oscillator with FEEDBACK, MULTI and NODE.
4. Record a sequence: turn on RECORD with NOTES (and BEATS or KNOBS if you like). Set each chord, then press FWD to move to the next stage.
5. Press PLAY.
6. Add space with the MIX and DELAY FX sections.
sections.patching:
• Play from a keyboard: Set VCV MIDI-CV to 6-note polyphony and send its V/oct and gate through POLY MAP into V/OCT. Chords you play fill all six voices.

[[fig:unison]]

• Several in unison: Run a few CHORD CASTERs from the same CLOCK TRIG. and RESET (VCV PUSH makes a handy sync button), with different OFFSET or SPREAD for a thick stereo stack.

• Your own oscillator: Set EXT. to Maps to VCA and patch a poly oscillator in. You keep CHORD CASTER's rhythm, envelopes, mixer and delay.

• Transposing by sequence: Set EXT. to Maps to V/Oct Offset and patch in a second sequencer.

• Plucked strings: BUFFER SIZE 36, REVERB high, short DELAY. The delay becomes a Karplus-Strong resonator.

• Strummed chords: Turn on STRUM and set NODES to ±1, so the six envelopes fire one after another every stage.

figures.caption: Areas 1–7: recorder, clock, transport, chord sequencer, notes, beat programmer and envelopes.
Areas 8–16: modulation, oscillator, mix, delay, strum and retrig, copy and paste, slew, inputs and outputs.
Several CHORD CASTERs in unison, played from a MIDI keyboard through POLY MAP.

name: Poly Map
tagline: Turns a poly MIDI signal into just the notes you're holding, ready for CHORD CASTER.

sections.panelMap:
POLY MAP connects polyphonic MIDI to CHORD CASTER. It reads a poly gate to see which notes are held and outputs only those pitches. The output's channel count changes with the number of notes, and CHORD CASTER spreads them across its six voices.

- POLY V/OCT IN: the poly pitches.
- POLY GATE IN: the matching poly gates.
- MAPPED V/OCT OUT: only the held notes. A single note is doubled, so the output always has at least two channels.
sections.basicUse:
1. Set VCV MIDI-CV to 6-note polyphony.
2. Patch its V/oct into POLY V/OCT IN and its gate into POLY GATE IN.
3. Patch MAPPED V/OCT OUT into CHORD CASTER's V/OCT.
4. Play chords. CHORD CASTER fills its six voices from the notes you hold.
sections.patching:
• Live chords: MIDI keyboard into CHORD CASTER through POLY MAP, as above.

• Tidy poly signals: Use POLY MAP before any module that works better with only the active notes, such as a chord quantizer like MIRAGE.

name: Chordy
tagline: CHORD CASTER's chord sequencer on its own, with separate outputs for each note and a ROTATE control.

sections.panelMap:
CHORDY is the chord-sequencing brain of CHORD CASTER in a smaller module, with a few extras. Separate outputs for all six notes make it easy to patch, and ROTATE gets more variety out of the same chords.

Sequencer (as on CHORD CASTER)
- STAGE and MAX: the current stage and the number of stages. The display shows both and the current chord.
- Keyboard and chord buttons: the root (with octave − and +) and one of 16 chord types.
- NOTE − and + for each voice: move single notes in the voicing.
- Beats per stage − and +: clock pulses per stage.
- RECORD and EDIT: record chord changes into stages, or load them for editing.
- COPY, COPY ALL, PASTE, CLEAR, ADD, DELETE: edit the sequence.
- On/off, RESET, REV and FWD, with inputs. CLOCK input to advance.

Inputs
- NOTE and CHORD: set the root and chord type by CV.
- External transpose: added to every note.
- ROTATE: see below.

ROTATE: turns the six notes around the outputs, by CV or with the trimpot. The red light shows which output has the first note of the chord.

Outputs
- STAGE: a trigger whenever the stage changes.
- MONO: six separate outputs, one per note.
- POLY: the same six notes as one poly cable.

Context menu
- Set Max Sequence Length.
- Stop Record At End.
sections.basicUse:
1. Pick a root on the keyboard and a chord type.
2. Clock it, and record chord changes into stages with RECORD.
3. Take POLY to a poly voice, or the six MONO outputs to six separate voices.
4. Turn ROTATE, or patch CV into it, to move the notes between outputs.
sections.patching:
• Six-voice orchestra: Send each MONO output to a different instrument, so every chord tone gets its own sound.

• Rotating voicings: Clock ROTATE from STAGE or an LFO so the same chords are passed around the voices.

• Chord tones as modulation: Patch the MONO outputs into filter cutoffs or pans for motion that follows the harmony.

• Driving CHORD CASTER: Patch POLY into CHORD CASTER's V/OCT to use CHORDY as an outboard chord source.

name: Dunes
tagline: Two function generators that rise, fall and wait. With curve shaping, phase gates, and MIN, SUM and MAX of both.

sections.panelMap:
DUNES is two function generators, I and II, mirrored on either side of a shared centre. Each one rises, falls, then waits before it can go again, so the rest between shapes is part of the rhythm. The centre combines the two into MIN, SUM and MAX, with a meter to watch them. All inputs are polyphonic.

Each side
- RANGE switch: Slow (0.4 s to 6.8 min), Mid (10 ms to 10 s, the default) or Fast (0.4 ms to 410 ms).
- MODE switch:
  - Slope: a gate starts the cycle and keeps it looping while high. Letting go during the rise cuts straight to the fall.
  - Sustain: a gate rises, holds at the peak while high, and falls when released.
  - Delay: wait first, then rise, then fall. Letting go during the wait cancels it. Holding the gate through the end loops back into the wait.
  A trigger always plays the whole rise, in every mode.
- RISE, FALL, WAIT sliders: the length of each stage, with trim and CV.
- GROW and DECAY sliders: the curve of the rise and the fall, from log through linear to exponential, with trim and CV.
- TRIG: input and button. Fires one full cycle.
- GATE: input and button.
- CYCLE: input and latching button (yellow). Loops continuously.
- Mixer knob (below the meter), with trim and CV: this side's level into OUT, MIN, SUM and MAX.

Centre
- Meter: columns for I, MIN, SUM, MAX and II.

Outputs (bottom row)
- OUT I and OUT II.
- RISE, FALL and WAIT gates for each side, high during that stage.
- MIN, SUM and MAX of the two sides.

Context menu
- Gate Comparator: the threshold for the GATE inputs, in volts.
- Cycle I Jack and Cycle II Jack: Toggle Mode. By default the CYCLE inputs loop only while high; in toggle mode each gate flips looping on or off.
sections.basicUse:
1. Choose a RANGE for each side.
2. Set RISE, FALL and WAIT.
3. Shape the stages with GROW and DECAY.
4. Fire it with TRIG, hold it with GATE, or press CYCLE to loop it.
5. Take OUT, or combine both sides with MIN, SUM and MAX.
sections.patching:
• Envelope: Mode on Sustain, a gate into GATE I, OUT I to a VCA.

• Related pair: Trigger both sides together with different GROW and DECAY. Send MAX to a filter and MIN to a VCA.

• LFOs with rests: CYCLE on, with some WAIT. The pause between shapes becomes part of the rhythm.

• Chains: Patch WAIT I into TRIG II and WAIT II into TRIG I so the two sides take turns.

• Drum triggers: Use the RISE and FALL gates to fire drums or step sequencers in time with the shapes.

• Poly envelopes: A poly gate gives each voice its own cycle.

name: Crosswinds
tagline: A sixteen-step gate sequencer where every step can be nudged early or late, or ratcheted.

sections.panelMap:
CROSSWINDS is a sixteen-step gate sequencer that works on timing. Each step can be pushed earlier or later than the beat, so the same pattern can swing, drag, rush or fall into polyrhythms. Switch the knobs to ratchet mode and each step can repeat up to nine times instead.

Steps
- 16 knobs in four beats, I to IV: offset each step, from a whole step early to a whole step late. In ratchet mode they set repeats, 1–9.
- 16 step buttons: turn each step on or off.
- KNOB MODE button: switches the knobs between offset and ratchet.
- Display: the displaced gate pattern, with a playback cursor. It dims, but stays editable, while stopped.

Global
- LENGTH slider, with attenuverter and CV: 1–16 steps.
- DEPTH slider, with attenuverter and CV: scales all the offsets together.
- CV MAP: a 16-channel poly input. Channel N controls step N. What it controls is set in the context menu.

Transport
- ON: starts and stops, with a button and input. Each start goes back to the first beat.
- BEAT: the clock input. With nothing patched, the button is a tap tempo. Starts at 120 BPM.
- RESET: back to the first beat, without stopping.

Outputs
- OUT: the displaced gates.
- END: a gate at the end of each loop, or at the end of a one-shot pass.

Context menu
- One-shot mode (vs. loop): plays through once, then stops.
- Gate Width: from a 1 ms trigger up to 99% of a beat.
- MAP CV Destination: Ratchets (default), Offsets or Step Gates.
- Step Gate CV: Toggle mode (vs. Direct Set), for when CV MAP drives the step gates.
sections.basicUse:
1. Patch a clock into BEAT, or tap the button.
2. Turn on the steps you want.
3. Turn the knobs to move steps early or late. Use DEPTH to scale everything at once.
4. Set LENGTH.
5. Press KNOB MODE and turn some knobs up for ratchets.
6. Take OUT to a drum, and END to anything that should happen once per loop.
sections.patching:
• Swing: Leave most offsets at 0 and push the off-beat steps slightly late.

• Displaced rhythm: Move alternate steps in opposite directions for patterns that sit across the beat.

• Ratchet fills: Set CV MAP to Ratchets and send a poly envelope or LFO in, so busy moments ratchet harder.

• Fills on cue: One-shot mode, with a trigger into ON to play the pattern once.

• Song sections: Use END to step a sequencer or trigger a new section every loop.

• Breathing groove: A slow LFO on DEPTH so the displacement drifts in and out.

name: Drifts
tagline: Four looping waveforms at clock ratios, mixed into one melodic line. Or run it at audio rate as an oscillator.

sections.panelMap:
DRIFTS runs four waveform layers, each looping at its own ratio of the clock, and adds them into one melodic CV. Each layer has its own pitch range, shape and phase, so together they make long, slowly shifting lines that still lock to tempo. It was made as a melody source for MIRAGE. Switch on V/oct mode and it becomes an audio oscillator.

Layers (four rows)
- Button and gate input: turns the layer on or off.
- CYCLES and BEATS: the layer loops CYCLES times every BEATS clock beats. 1:2 is one loop every two beats.
- MIN and MAX: the layer's range, ±48 semitones. The display shows the ratio and range.
- Wave display: the layer's waveform, with a dot for its position.
- WAVE SHAPE slider, with trim and CV: picks one of 16 shapes from the current wave set.
- PHASE slider, with trim and CV: starting offset of the layer.

Global
- WAVE SET knob and CV: morphs between three families of wave shapes, wrapping round.
- SYNC TYPE buttons: RATIO rounds the cycle lengths to whole numbers so the layers stay aligned. OSC. syncs the layers to each other (soft or hard sync, set in the context menu).
- REVERSE: runs the layers backwards, with a button and gate input.
- ON: runs and stops.
- V: V/oct mode. CLOCK then reads pitch instead of tempo.
- RESET: resets every layer.
- OFFSET: shifts the output, ±5V, with CV.
- CV MAP: a poly input that can drive many layer controls at once (see the context menu).
- CLOCK: clock, or pitch in V/oct mode.

Output
- CV RANGE switch: what happens at the edges of the output window. Wrap, Reflect or Clip.
- MIN and MAX: the output window, ±48 semitones.
- MIX OUT: the four layers added together.
- 1–4: each layer on its own.
- POLY: all four as one poly cable.

Context menu
- CV Map: assigns each group of four poly channels (1–4, 5–8, 9–12, 13–16) to a layer control: Phase, Wave Shape, Range Min, Range Max, Ratio Cycles, Ratio Beats or Layer Gate.
- Gate CV Mode: Momentary or Toggle for the layer gates.
- Reverse CV Mode: Momentary or Toggle.
- Oscillator Sync Mode: Soft Sync or Hard Sync.
- Output Modes: what the layer outputs and the poly output carry. Phasor (0–10V), Layer CV (semitone scaled), or Layer CV (bipolar ±5V).
- Oversampling Factor: Off, 2x (default), 4x or 8x, with a Filter Cutoff slider, for audio-rate use.
sections.basicUse:
1. Patch a clock into CLOCK and press ON.
2. Set CYCLES and BEATS for each layer to choose how fast it loops.
3. Set each layer's MIN and MAX range, and the output window.
4. Pick shapes with WAVE SHAPE and the WAVE SET knob.
5. Turn layers on and off to thin or thicken the line.
6. Take MIX OUT into a quantizer, such as MIRAGE.
sections.patching:
• Melody for MIRAGE: MIX OUT into MIRAGE's CV input. Slow ratios give wandering lines that stay in key.

• Four related LFOs: Use the layer outputs on their own, with different ratios.

• Poly modulation: POLY into a poly destination, with Output Modes on Phasor or bipolar.

• Audio oscillator: Turn on V and patch a pitch into CLOCK. Use OSC. sync and different ratios for sync-style timbres, and raise oversampling.

• Play the layers: A gate pattern into the layer gates brings layers in and out in rhythm.

name: Arcs
tagline: An 8×8 router that rolls the dice. Each trigger crossfades to a new random set of connections.

sections.panelMap:
ARCS routes eight inputs to eight outputs at random. Each trigger picks a new set of connections and crossfades to it. Four sliders set the odds: how many inputs and outputs take part, how much crosstalk there is, and how long the fades last. The display draws every connection as an arc.

Sliders (each with an attenuverter and CV)
- IN: chance that each input takes part. At the top, every patched input plays.
- CROSS: chance of extra arcs between inputs and outputs that aren't paired, for crosstalk.
- FADE: crossfade time, up to 4 seconds. At 0 the routing switches instantly.
- OUT: chance that each output receives a signal.

Jacks
- Inputs 1–8 (left). A poly cable in input 1 spreads across the inputs.
- Outputs 1–8 (right).
- TRIG: input and button. Picks a new routing.
- HOLD: input and button. Freezes the current routing.
- FADE output: an envelope that rises from 0V to 10V across each crossfade.

Context menu
- IN/OUT: guarantee at least 1 active. On by default.
- FADE: Random time in [0, max]. Off by default, so every fade takes the FADE time exactly.
- Hold CV: Latching Toggle. By default HOLD only holds while its gate is high.
- Randomize routing now.
- Reset to identity routing (1→1, 2→2, …).
sections.basicUse:
1. Patch sources into the inputs and destinations from the outputs.
2. Set IN and OUT for how many take part, and CROSS for crosstalk.
3. Set FADE.
4. Send triggers to TRIG for new routings.
5. Hold a routing you like with HOLD.
sections.patching:
• Changing effects sends: Dry sources and effect returns into the inputs; each trigger makes a new mix.

• Slowly morphing textures: Several oscillators or noise voices in, long FADE, occasional triggers.

• Poly spread: A poly source into input 1, scattered across the outputs.

• Events in step: Patch the FADE output into a comparator to fire something when each crossfade finishes.

• Mostly still: Leave HOLD on, and release it now and then for a surprise.

name: Mirage
tagline: A chord-aware melody quantizer. Plays the chord tones, then adds passing notes, including just and microtonal ones, as you turn up EXPRESSION.

sections.panelMap:
MIRAGE quantizes a melody to the chord that's playing, then expands the chord into a scale. Passing notes are ranked by how well they suit the chord, and EXPRESSION lets them in, most useful first. With the tuning set to Just or Pythagorean, the passing notes can sit between the keys of a piano.

Display
- Keyboard: the chord. Click keys to set it by hand, or patch a chord into CHORD.
- Strip: chord tones (bright) and active passing notes (dimmer), placed on the current tuning grid. The top passing notes are labelled by interval or ratio, like 7/4 or 6/5. They turn grey while GATE is closed.
- Chord name: below the keyboard.

Controls
- ROOT: picks the root. With no chord patched, it picks among the chord tones.
- EXPRESSION: how many passing notes are allowed. At 0 only chord tones.
- MODE: the tuning of the passing notes. 12T (semitones only), JUST (ratios of the harmonic series from the root), PYTH (stacked pure fifths, with wide, tense thirds), 24T (quarter tones).

Inputs
- ROOT: root note as V/oct.
- EXP.: EXPRESSION CV, 0–10V.
- CHORD: poly V/oct chord.
- GATE: high allows passing notes, low allows chord tones only. Unpatched, it's open.
- CV: the melody to quantize.
- TRIG: sample and hold. Each trigger latches every output until the next.
- MODE has CV too, through its jack: 0–2.5V 12-TET, 2.5–5V Just, 5–7.5V Pythagorean, 7.5–10V 24-TET.

Outputs
- LEAD: the quantized melody.
- TENSION: the melody quantized to the full extended scale, ignoring GATE.
- DELTA: TENSION minus LEAD. It reads how hard the scale is holding the melody back.
- BEND: how far LEAD sits from 12-TET, up to a quarter tone. Send LEAD to a normal oscillator and BEND to its fine tune to keep the microtones.
- VEL.: 10V for chord tones, 1–9V for passing notes by rank.
- TRIG: fires whenever a new note is quantized.

The quantizer leans the way the melody is moving, so a rising line snaps up and a falling line snaps down. A sine LFO into CV runs cleanly up and down the scale.

Context menu
- Adaptive tuning: off by default, so microtonal notes are added alongside the chord as flavour notes. Turn it on and they replace the tempered chord tones, so the chord itself retunes toward just intonation as EXPRESSION rises.
- Delta as modulation (x20): scales DELTA up to about ±5V for filters and VCAs. Leave it off when DELTA goes to a pitch input.
sections.basicUse:
1. Set a chord on the keyboard, or patch a poly chord into CHORD.
2. Patch your melody into CV and take LEAD to an oscillator.
3. Start with EXPRESSION at 0 to hear chord tones only, then turn it up to let in passing notes.
4. Choose a MODE. Try JUST and PYTH for notes between the keys, and patch BEND to the oscillator's fine tune.
5. Use a gate to switch passing notes on for some phrases and off for others.
sections.patching:
• Lead over chord changes: WEAVE's POLY or CHORD CASTER's NOTES into CHORD. Sweep EXPRESSION with an envelope to add colour only at the peaks of phrases.

• DRIFTS into MIRAGE: DRIFTS' MIX OUT into CV for wandering lines that always fit the chord.

• Natural phrasing: VEL. into an envelope's level. Chord tones land hard, passing notes are softer.

• A second voice: TENSION into another oscillator for a line that always uses the full scale.

• Tension as modulation: Turn on Delta as modulation and send DELTA to a filter. It opens when the melody pushes against the scale.

• Just chords: MODE on JUST with Adaptive tuning on. As EXPRESSION rises, the chord itself settles into pure intervals.

name: Sirocco
tagline: A desert in a module. Grass grows, locusts swarm, the wind blows and it rains, and every part of it is a CV output.

sections.panelMap:
SIROCCO simulates a small desert ecosystem. Grass grows and spreads its seeds on the wind. Locusts find the grass and multiply, eat it faster than it can recover, and crash. The grass grows back and it starts again. This is the classic predator-prey (Lotka-Volterra) cycle, but it plays out along a strip of 64 patches of ground, so different places are at different stages at the same time. Swarms form, move, strip an area bare and dissolve somewhere else. The outputs never quite repeat.

The display shows the strip: grass in gold, moisture in blue, seeds, and the locust swarm in green, under the night sky.

Weather (knob, attenuverter and CV)
- WIND: how much energy the weather has. Sets how far seeds blow and how strong storms get.
- SQUALL: how changeable the wind is: how often it changes direction, and how often dust storms come.

Ecology (sliders, each with CV)
- BLOOM: how fast grass grows back.
- WILT: drought. Grass dies off on its own, without locusts. This unsettles the cycle and makes it less regular.
- CYCLE (centre, ⟳): the master tempo of the whole predator-prey cycle.
- EAT: how fast locusts turn grass into more locusts.
- GROW: how long locusts survive without food.

Events (button and trigger input)
- STORM: a dust storm. A surge of wind that scatters the seeds.
- RAIN: a rainfall. Grass blooms across the strip.
- WADI: switches the strip between a loop (the ends join) and a valley with walls at each end.
- RESET: back to a sparse desert.

Outputs
- GRASS: total grass, 0–10V.
- SEED: a 1 ms trigger each time grass seeds itself.
- POLY: grass density along the strip, in 16 channels, 0–10V.
- WIND: wind speed and direction, ±5V.
- RAIN: rain and storm intensity, 0–10V.
- POP.: locust population, 0–10V.
- SWARM: where the swarm is along the strip, 0–10V.

Context menu
- Seed Timing: Seed maturation rate, and the Re-seed die-back threshold.
- RAIN Output Mode: Intensity (default), Rain gate, or Dust storm gate.
sections.basicUse:
1. Let it run. At the default settings the ecosystem organises itself. Watch the grass grow, the swarms bloom and the rain fall.
2. Change the weather with WIND and SQUALL, or press RAIN and STORM.
3. Change the life cycle: BLOOM for how quickly grass recovers, EAT and GROW for how locusts boom and bust, WILT for drought, CYCLE for the overall speed.
4. Press WADI to switch between a looped strip and a walled valley.
5. Patch the outputs. GRASS and POP. move in opposite directions, SWARM moves along the strip, and WIND swings both ways.
sections.patching:
• Paired slow LFOs: GRASS to a filter cutoff and POP. to a reverb mix. As one rises the other falls.

• Moving sound: SWARM into a panner. The sound follows the locusts across the stereo field.

• Weather events: Set RAIN to Rain gate and use it to open a reverb or sweep a filter. Use SEED to pluck strings or fire percussion.

• Drift: WIND, attenuated, into a pitch or delay time for slow, organic movement.

• Sixteen lanes: POLY into 16 VCA levels or brightness controls for a field of moving amplitudes.

name: Zephyr
tagline: A polyphonic oscillator and LFO with three families of waveforms, morphable in two directions.

sections.panelMap:
ZEPHYR is a polyphonic oscillator and LFO built on three families of waveforms, arranged as a space you can move through in two directions. WAVE picks one of 16 shapes in a family, and WAVE SET moves between the three families, blending them in between. Both wrap around at the ends, so you can keep going forever.

- Set A: classic shapes. Pulses, saws, arches and spikes.
- Set B: harmonic and tonal shapes. Fourier series, formants and spectral sweeps.
- Set C: rhythmic and melodic gestures. Bitcrushed staircases, supersaws, zigzags and holds.
WAVE SET has soft detents at A, B and C, so it's easy to land on a pure family.

The display shows the current waveform for the first voice. At LFO rates a dot follows the playhead.

Sliders (each with trim and CV)
- WAVE SET: moves between families A, B and C.
- WAVE: moves through the 16 shapes.
- PHASE: offsets the start of the wave. Poly CV sets it per voice.
- FILTER: a low-pass after the shaper. Above about 0.8 it's out of the way; at LFO rates it's off.

Pitch
- RANGE switch: Audio, Low (6 octaves down) or Slow (12 octaves down, for LFOs).
- Big knob: frequency, ±4V.
- V/OCT: polyphonic, up to 16 voices.

FM and sync
- EXP: exponential FM input, with trim.
- LIN: linear through-zero FM input, with amount knob.
- HARD: hard sync. A rising edge restarts the wave.
- SOFT: soft sync. A rising edge reverses the wave's direction.

Outputs
- PHASOR: the oscillator's phase as a 0–10V ramp, polyphonic.
- OUT: the audio, polyphonic.

Context menu
- Output Range: ±5V (default), ±10V, 0–10V or 0–5V.
- Supersampling, and Oversampling Factor (Off, 2x default, 4x, 8x).
sections.basicUse:
1. Patch a poly V/oct into V/OCT. Use the knob to tune and RANGE for the octave.
2. Pick a family with WAVE SET and a shape with WAVE.
3. Modulate WAVE and WAVE SET to move through the shapes.
4. Use FILTER to soften the top end.
5. For an LFO, set RANGE to Slow and leave V/OCT unpatched. The knob sets the rate.
sections.patching:
• Poly synth: Poly V/oct from a sequencer or MIDI. A poly envelope on WAVE gives each note its own timbre, and a slow LFO on WAVE SET moves the whole sound.

• Two-way morphing: Two LFOs at different rates into WAVE and WAVE SET. The timbre keeps evolving without obvious repeats.

• Shaped LFO: RANGE on Slow. Set C gives rhythmic, gate-like contours; Set B gives smooth movement.

• FM pair: One ZEPHYR's OUT into another's LIN, with the amount knob set to taste.

• Sync sweep: One ZEPHYR's PHASOR into a second one's HARD, tuned higher. Sweep the second one's WAVE and WAVE SET while it's synced.

• Ramp source: PHASOR is a clean 0–10V ramp following the pitch, for waveshapers and scanners.

name: Droplet
tagline: A strikeable resonator ring feeding a plate reverb, with clickable node modes, FM, and dynamics that move the sliders for you.

sections.panelMap:
DROPLET is two physical models joined together: a ring of eight resonating nodes (the drop) feeding an eight-node plate reverb (the plate). Strike the ring for bells, tines and cymbals, or feed it audio and use it as a resonant reverb. Everything is polyphonic. The poly input with the most channels sets the voice count, and an input with fewer channels holds its last channel for the voices above it.

How it works
- The drop: each node is a tuned delay line with gentle saturation and its own compression. The eight nodes are spread across the stereo field. TEMPER couples each node to its neighbours.
- The plate: a network of allpass delays mixed together, shaped by PLATE, DIFFUSE, COUPLE, DECAY and DAMP.
- SHIMMER links the two. It slowly drifts the tuning of each node, which keeps the ring from building up on one note, and it raises extra connections: across the ring, across the plate, and from the plate back into the ring, following the lines on the panel. At zero those connections are off; turned up, the two models exchange more and more energy and the sound gets bigger and more complex.

Inputs (left)
- PITCH: knob and V/oct input for the ring's pitch, polyphonic.
- FM: input and FM amount trimmer, between PITCH and DROP IN. Exponential FM of the ring's pitch, polyphonic. The trimmer is tapered so small amounts get most of its travel (25% ≈ 0.016 oct/V, 50% ≈ 0.125, 100% = 1 oct/V). FM skips the pitch glide, so audio-rate FM works.
- DROP IN L/R: audio into the ring.
- PLATE IN L/R: audio straight into the plate.
- STRIKE: trigger input and button. Polyphonic triggers strike each voice separately; the button strikes them all.

The grid (centre)
- Sixteen lights: the top two rows are the drop's nodes, the bottom two the plate's. The large light is the node's energy and the small white light its detuning. The grid shows the first voice.
- Every light is also a button that changes the node's mode. Modes are shared by all voices, saved with the patch, and crossfade when you click them. Hover over a node to see its mode.
  - Drop nodes: Normal (blue) or Hollow (white). A Hollow node flips its feedback and halves its delay, so it rings at the same pitch with odd harmonics only, like a tube or a clarinet. Hollow nodes ring much longer and bloom: they're held up at a steady level, then let go once they fade below a threshold.
  - Plate nodes: Normal (orange), Long (pink) or Short (yellow). Long reads the line at 4× its length for later reflections and a longer tail. Short reads it at ¼, a tight comb with a metallic, boxy ring.
- Eight node trims around the circle offset each drop node's tuning. The ? button randomizes them and the 0 button zeros them.

Mix (top right)
- WET: dry to wet, with trim and CV.
- BLEND: the wet sound, from pure ring (zero) to pure plate (full), with trim and CV. In between, the ring is mixed in inverted, as it would be physically, which gives a natural comb-like colour.
- VOL.: output level, with CV.

Outputs
- OUTPUTS L/R: stereo, polyphonic.
- DROP: the ring's level as an envelope, 0–10V, per voice. Blue meter.
- STRIKE: the strike's envelope, 0–10V, per voice. Yellow meter.

Sliders (bottom, each with trim and CV)
- Drop (blue): SHAPE (how the nodes are spread: unison, spread, spread into chaos, pure chaos), SHIMMER, TEMPER, RES. (how long the ring sustains).
- Plate (yellow): DIFFUSE (density), PLATE (spacing and scatter of the plate nodes), COUPLE (energy shared between plate nodes), DECAY (tail length), DAMP (rolls off the highs in ring and plate; it fades in over the bottom quarter, then sweeps from 8 kHz down to 200 Hz).
- DYNAMICS (white): how much, and which way, the dynamics follower moves the sliders.

Dynamics
- The buttons above the first nine sliders choose which ones the dynamics follower moves.
- The button above DYNAMICS chooses the source: DROP level (blue), STRIKE envelope (yellow), or off.

Context menu
- Node Modes: Drop nodes (All Normal, All Hollow, Checkerboard, Randomize), Plate nodes (All Normal, All Long, All Short, Checkerboard Long / Short, Randomize), Randomize all node modes, Reset all node modes. The submenus show how many nodes are in each mode.
- Dynamics Envelope: Follow Time.
- Auto Rand. Thresh. and Rand. Range: randomize the node trims automatically when the ring gets loud enough, and set how far.
- Resonator Gain: drive inside the ring.
- Strike Character: Strike Length, Slant, Curve, Strike Intensity and Noise.
- Plate Seed (0–99999) and Re-roll Plate Character: each seed is a different plate.
- Panic: Clear All Energy.
sections.basicUse:
1. Strike it:
   - Set the pitch, then press STRIKE or patch triggers in. A poly V/oct and poly triggers give each note its own ring and plate.

2. Shape the ring:
   - SHAPE from unison to chaos, RES. for sustain, TEMPER to blend the nodes, SHIMMER to link ring and plate.

3. Shape the plate:
   - DIFFUSE, PLATE, COUPLE and DECAY set the space. DAMP darkens both.

4. Set the mix:
   - BLEND chooses between ring and plate; WET mixes in the dry sound. For a plain reverb send, set BLEND to full plate.

5. Feed it audio:
   - DROP IN excites the ring; PLATE IN goes straight to the plate.

6. Change the nodes:
   - Click drop nodes for Hollow, and plate nodes for Long or Short.

7. Add FM:
   - Patch a modulator into FM and raise the trimmer.

8. Let the dynamics play:
   - Light some DYN buttons, choose a source, and raise DYNAMICS.
sections.patching:
• Plate reverb: Audio into DROP IN, BLEND at full plate, WET to taste. Shape the tail with DIFFUSE and DECAY.

• Resonator: BLEND at zero and strike it, or feed it audio. A tuned comb or metallic resonator.

• Bells and tines: Leave the inputs empty, sequence PITCH and trigger STRIKE.

• Big steel: SHIMMER at 0.5–0.8. The ring and plate trade energy for long, complex, inharmonic decays.

• Cymbals: DAMP at zero, DECAY at 0.9, SHIMMER at 0.6–0.8, then press ? to randomize the trims.

• Hollow tubes: All drop nodes Hollow. Same pitch, odd harmonics only, with a long bloom.

• Long hall or metal box: All plate nodes Long for a bigger space; a few Short for a tight metallic ring on top.

• Bowed drone: An audio-rate gate into STRIKE keeps exciting the ring. Shape it with Strike Length and Slant.

• Reactive reverb: Drums into DROP IN, source on DROP (blue), DECAY's DYN button on. Loud hits lengthen the tail.

• Per-voice envelopes: Use STRIKE out to drive a VCA or filter for each voice.

• Audio-rate FM: An oscillator on the same V/oct into FM, trimmer at 25–40%, for gong and bell sidebands.

name: Strands
tagline: A hurdy-gurdy: six strings bowed by a rosined wheel, twelve sympathetic strings, and the buzzing chien.

sections.panelMap:
STRANDS is a physical model of a hurdy-gurdy. A turning wheel bows six strings at once. Two melody strings (chanterelles) follow V/oct and play left and right. Three drone strings (mouche, bourdon and trompette) sit at fixed intervals below the root. Twelve sympathetic strings, in six tuned pairs, ring along with the bowed strings. The trompette rests on the chien, a loose bridge that buzzes when you push the wheel harder, the hurdy-gurdy's signature rattle.

The wheel is a real rosined wheel, not a perfect one. Its surface repeats with every turn:
- Unevenness: broad high and low spots, the same for every string, so the instrument swells and dips once per turn.
- Grit: the rosin's grain. Each string runs on its own track across the wheel, catching and releasing on its own.
- Wobble: slow variation in the crank speed, from the player's hand. It fades out at very low speeds, so a stopped wheel really stops.
The bow's grip also follows the wheel speed, so a faster wheel is louder but keeps the clean sawtooth motion of a bowed string instead of turning thin and reedy.

The display shows the melody string, fixed at both ends, with an ellipse for the wheel's contact point and speed. It warms from blue-grey to amber as you bow harder and add DRIVE.

Stereo: the two chanterelles and the two trompettes each have their own chain (saturation and body resonator), one per side. The other drones and the sympathetic strings sit in the middle.

Sliders (each with trim and CV)
- TONE: brightness at the bridge, 300 Hz to 18 kHz.
- DRIVE: saturation after the strings, before the body.
- POS.: where the wheel touches the string. Low is round; high is bright and nasal, near the bridge.
- SYMP.: how much the sympathetic strings ring.

Knobs and jacks
- Big knob: melody pitch (±1V around C4), with V/OCT below. The drones follow the knob only, not V/OCT.
- BOW: wheel speed, -2 to +2, with trim and CV. Negative turns the wheel backwards. At zero the module sleeps.
- TIRANT: input and trim. Pushes on the chien; at zero it stays silent.
- VOL.: volume, with CV.
- FM: input and trim. FM on the melody strings; depth in semitones is set in the context menu.
- OUT L / R.

Context menu
- Bow Junction: Sticking Friction, Slip Falloff, Capture Velocity and String Impedance. These are the grip of the bow. They're set for a moderate wheel speed and scale with it above that.
- Drone Strings: Drone Mix Level, and the Mouche, Bourdon and Trompette intervals below the root.
- Melody / FM: FM Depth, and 2nd Chanterelle Detune (cents) for beating and width.
- Sympathetic Strings (12, 6 pairs): Max Coupling, Sympathetic Decay, Sympathetic Damping, Pair Spread (the two strings in a pair sit this many cents apart, so they beat slowly like a real course), and the interval of each pair.
- Wheel: Grit, Unevenness and Wobble.
- Body: Body Feedback and Body Diffusion, the resonance of the instrument's body.
- Trompette Chien: Enable, the Chien Pulse (Width and Amplitude of the rattle), Trigger Depth at Full Tirant, and 2nd Trompette Detune (which puts the buzz in stereo).
- Panic: Clear All Energy.
sections.basicUse:
1. Turn the wheel:
   - Turn up BOW. The strings start once the wheel is fast enough. An envelope into BOW CV makes each note bloom.

2. Play a melody:
   - Patch V/oct into V/OCT. The drones stay on the root set by the big knob.

3. Shape the tone:
   - TONE for brightness, POS. for where the wheel touches, DRIVE for grit.
   - The Bow Junction menu sets the grip. Less capture and more slip falloff sound crisper, and the display's wave sharpens toward a sawtooth.

4. Add the buzz:
   - Patch a CV into TIRANT. The chien fires when the trompette's vibration dips below a level set by the tirant. Zero never fires; more fires more often; past full it buzzes constantly.
   - Each fire is a short rattle of shrinking bounces. Chien Pulse Width and Amplitude set its length and level.
   - Two chiens, one per trompette, fire at slightly different times, so the buzz is in stereo.

5. Add the sympathetic strings:
   - Raise SYMP. They're tuned to the bowed strings' notes and hear the chanterelles fully and the drones lightly. They bloom when the melody lands on one of their notes.

6. Shape the wheel and body:
   - Wheel menu: Grit for a rough, rosiny catch, Unevenness for a swell on every turn, Wobble for hand drift. Set all three to zero for a perfectly smooth wheel.
   - Body menu: Body Feedback for sustain and a boxy warmth, Body Diffusion for its colour.

7. If it locks up on high notes:
   - Notes above about +2V fold down an octave automatically. If it still saturates, use Panic.
sections.patching:
• Melody over drones: V/oct into V/OCT, an envelope into BOW. The melody speaks on each note over a constant drone.

• Drone only: BOW at a fixed level, nothing in V/OCT. Use SYMP. and Body Feedback to fill it out.

• Expressive bowing: A mod wheel or expression pedal into BOW. Slow is fragile and breathy; fast is loud and saturated.

• Rhythmic buzz: A stepped sequence into TIRANT so the chien buzzes on some notes and not others.

• Vibrato or sitar: A little LFO on FM for vibrato. More FM Depth and a faster LFO gives metallic, sitar-like tones.

• Sympathetic bloom: SYMP. high, and the six pairs tuned to notes of your scale. Raise Pair Spread for a wider, slower shimmer.

• Sul ponticello: POS. near the top, TONE bright, a little DRIVE, and less Capture Velocity, for a nasal folk fiddle.
